recipes.title: Oat Porridge
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Breakfast recipes|servings=1|time=15 minutes|difficulty=2|image=[[Image:Oatmealraisins2.jpg|300px|Oatmeal with raisins]]}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast]]

'''Porridge''' (also known in American English as '''hot cereal'''), is a simple dish made by boiling [[Cookbook:Grain|grain]] (often [[Cookbook:Rolled Oats|rolled oats]]) in water or milk. Porridge made from Irish oats, also called steel-cut oats, takes longer to cook—typically 15–20 minutes.

==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (45 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) rolled [[Cookbook:Oats|oats]] or other grain
* ¾ cup (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* ¾ cup (180 ml) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

==Procedure==
#Mix oats and water, then bring to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], covered with a lid.
#Once bubbling, stir and reduce temperature to the lowest possible to maintain [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmering]]. Replace lid and watch carefully to prevent boiling over.
#Stir every minute or so. After five minutes, remove lid, stir thoroughly and add milk.
#Mix through, and keep stirring until fully mixed.
#Serve and add [[cookbook:raisin|raisins]], [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]], [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]], [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]], a pinch of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] or inverted sugar syrup to taste.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Soak whole grains over night and change water. Soaking softens the grains and reduces cooking time, although whole oats still require 45–60 minutes simmering. Rinsing also reduces starch and pesticide residue. Steel cut oats should simmer for 20–30 minutes, or to the desired texture. Let the water boil out for a chewier, rice-like flavor with whole oats or leave some water in as is common with rolled oats and instant oats.
* Porridge can be made using water, milk, or a mixing of the two depending on taste. Other ingredients may include [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], [[Cookbook:Date|dates]], [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]], [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], and [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]. Add apples and cinnamon during the cooking process to infuse the flavor. If you want to avoid milk products, it is also possible to use [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]] instead of cow's milk. Corn oil also works well with honey and figs, out of the vegetable oils. Honey itself combines well with apples and cinnamon while raisins, dates, and bananas are popular with dairy ingredients. Winter squash can be added to finer grains like wheat and millet.
* 3 tbsp (90 ml) of milk powder or non-dairy milk powder can replace liquid milk by increasing water to 1½ cups (360 ml)
* Porridge was traditionally cooked over a wooden fire and in a cast iron pot which prevents burning and doesn't interfere with the flavor. In modern times, any pot will do as long as it is thick enough to distribute the heat. 
* Instant oats are the easiest and fastest to cook as they only need boiling water and as this may be also done with a microwave oven.

steps_original: Mix oats and water, then bring to the boil, covered with a lid.
Once bubbling, stir and reduce temperature to the lowest possible to maintain simmering. Replace lid and watch carefully to prevent boiling over.
Stir every minute or so. After five minutes, remove lid, stir thoroughly and add milk.
Mix through, and keep stirring until fully mixed.
Serve and add raisins, sugar, brown sugar, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, honey or inverted sugar syrup to taste.

Rinsing also reduces starch and pesticide residue. Steel cut oats should simmer for 20–30 minutes, or to the desired texture. Let the water boil out for a chewier, rice-like flavor with whole oats or leave some water in as is common with rolled oats and instant oats.
* Porridge can be made using water, milk, or a mixing of the two depending on taste. Other ingredients may include [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], [[Cookbook:Date|dates]], [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]], [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], and [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]. Add apples and cinnamon during the cooking process to infuse the flavor. If you want to avoid milk products, it is also possible to use [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]] instead of cow's milk. Corn oil also works well with honey and figs, out of the vegetable oils. Honey itself combines well with apples and cinnamon while raisins, dates, and bananas are popular with dairy ingredients. Winter squash can be added to finer grains like wheat and millet.
* 3 tbsp (90 ml) of milk powder or non-dairy milk powder can replace liquid milk by increasing water to 1½ cups (360 ml)
* Porridge was traditionally cooked over a wooden fire and in a cast iron pot which prevents burning and doesn't interfere with the flavor. In modern times, any pot will do as long as it is thick enough to distribute the heat. 
* Instant oats are the easiest and fastest to cook as they only need boiling water and as this may be also done with a microwave oven.

recipes.title: Garlic and Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Salad dressing recipes|servings=4|time=10 minutes|difficulty=1
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Salad Recipes|Salad Recipes]] 

'''Vinaigrette''' (from French ''vinaigre'', vinegar) is an emulsion of acid and fat, usually with other flavorings. It is one of the most basic salad dressings.

==Ingredients==
* 1 clove of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], smashed
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] prepared [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* 6 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]] ([[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]], extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive]], almond, hazelnut, etc.)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Spices and Herbs|Herbs]] to taste

==Procedure==
# Mix garlic, salt, mustard, and vinegar until smooth.
# Add oil and mix until smooth.
# Add pepper and herbs to taste.
# Let stand; the longer the herbs and mustard soak in the oil, the better-blended the flavor will be. You may need to quickly remix the vinaigrette just before dressing the salad if the oil and vinegar have separated while standing.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* The classical ratio of vinegar to oil is 1:3. Some recipes, however, suggest a ratio as low as 1:5.
* It is important to mix the mustard and vinegar first, then add the oil.  This helps the emulsion hold better, resulting in a smooth vinaigrette that is slow to separate out. Adding the oil in a stream and mixing as it is added helps even more.
* Use a pleasantly-flavored vinegar such as balsamic vinegar or red wine vinegar.
* Mustard powder may be used instead of regular prepared mustard.
* Instead of the garlic, a similar amount of very finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] shallot may be used.
* [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] the dressing with a salad just before serving. Greens that have been dressed wilt and become unappetizing within a few minutes.
* Different oils can be used for different flavors. Some suggest the use of vegetable oil, but this tends to add little in the way of flavor and most would find it unsuitable. Extra-virgin olive oil is always a good choice, but nearly any plant oil can be used, and experimentation is always good.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Pasta recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
* 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] whole grain thin [[Cookbook:Pasta|spaghetti]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] mild or hot Italian [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] red or dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 2 cans (28 ounces) no-salt-added [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 can (6 ounces) no-salt-added tomato paste
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 tsp dried [[Cookbook:Italian Seasoning|Italian seasoning]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]

==Procedure==
# Prepare [[cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] according to package directions.
# Meanwhile, heat oil in a 4½-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]] over medium-high heat.
# Peel and finely [[Cookbook:Chop|chop]] onion, adding to pan as you chop.
# Remove casings from sausage, if necessary, and [[cookbook:Crumble|crumble]] sausage into the pan. Stir and cook, breaking up the sausage, until the sausage is cooked through and the onion is tender, about 5 minutes.
# Add wine to pan and stir to loosen any brown bits on the bottom of the pan.
# Add canned tomatoes and their juice, tomato paste, garlic, sugar and Italian seasoning.
# Stir to combine, then reduce heat to medium-low.
# Stir in Parmesan cheese, and cook until pasta is ready.
# Serve the sauce with the cooked pasta.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* May substitute ½ cup chopped onion for small onion.
* Sauce can [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] on low, after cheese is added, up to 30 minutes, if necessary.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| Category = Vegetarian recipes
| Servings = 6–8
| Time = 60 minutes
| Rating = 2
<!--| Energy      = -->| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:RadishPie250px.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Radish tart''' is a tasty and colorful [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]], best served hot from the oven. Fresh red radishes and yellow cheese give this pretty pie an interesting look and taste.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*½ cup cold [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
*1 cup (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]], divided ([[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|Cheddar]] is also acceptable)
*1 cup heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]], divided
*4 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]] yolks
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*½–1 small bunch of red [[Cookbook:radish|radishes]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (220°C).
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
#Turn the dough into a 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] round [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]]. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie shell for 10–12 minutes. The sides will slip down a little during baking. Cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]].
#Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).
#Sprinkle the remaining cheese evenly over the bottom of the cooled pie shell. [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] together the egg yolks, the ¾ cup cream, and the salt. Pour the egg mixture over the cheese. Place the radish slices evenly over the top of the pie.
#Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until set.
#Remove the pie from the oven, cut it into wedges, and serve it hot. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*If you really like the taste of radishes, use ½ cup or more. For a milder pie, use ¼ cup.
*The cheese crust has a pleasant crisp texture when eaten fresh out of the oven. Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated later, but the texture will not be as good.
*A really sharp knife will aid in cutting the wedges without displacing the radishes.

ingredients_original: 1 cup (4 oz) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere cheese, divided (Cheddar is also acceptable)
½–1 small bunch of red radishes
steps_original: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).

Sift and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; toss the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
Turn the dough into a 9-inch round pie pan. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
Bake the pie shell for 10–12 minutes. The sides will slip down a little during baking. Cool on a wire rack.
Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).

Sprinkle the remaining cheese evenly over the bottom of the cooled pie shell. Beat together the egg yolks, the ¾ cup cream, and the salt. Pour the egg mixture over the cheese. Place the radish slices evenly over the top of the pie.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until set.
Remove the pie from the oven, cut it into wedges, and serve it hot.

*The cheese crust has a pleasant crisp texture when eaten fresh out of the oven. Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated later, but the texture will not be as good.
*A really sharp knife will aid in cutting the wedges without displacing the radishes.

recipes.title: Hot and Sour Soup
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| cactegory = Soup recipes
| servings = 4 persons
| time = 15–20 minutes
| difficulty = 2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Soup|Soup]]

'''Hot and sour soup''' is a popular soup served at Chinese restaurants in the United States. This version tastes exactly like that served at various Chinese restaurants in California.

==Ingredients==
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock or broth]] (or 4 cups water and 4 chicken [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|bouillon cubes]])
* 4 ½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] cooked shredded chicken or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* ¾ tablespoon garlic [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|chili sauce]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] freshly-ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* ⅓ cup white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* ½ cup canned [[Cookbook:Bamboo Shoot|bamboo shoots]], [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]]
* 4 ½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] block of [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]], cut into ¼-inch dice
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] and 2 tablespoons cold water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], beaten
* 3 [[Cookbook:Scallion|green onion]] stalks, diced (including tops)
* ¾ teaspoon toasted [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]

==Procedure==
# Bring chicken broth to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] in a 2-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# Add soy sauce, shredded meat, mushrooms and garlic chili sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes.
# Add black pepper, white vinegar, bamboo shoots, tofu. Simmer for 5 minutes.
# Combine 3 tablespoons of cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of cold water in a cup. Stir until mixture is smooth. Add cornstarch mixture to soup and stir well.
# Simmer for 5 minutes until soup is thickened.
# Beat egg in a cup until yolk and white are combined. Pour beaten egg slowly, in a fine stream into soup. Stir soup several times, then wait 30 seconds.
# Add green onions and sesame oil to soup. Stir well and remove from heat.
# Serve hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Adjust vinegar, ground black pepper, garlic chili sauce and soy sauce to taste. American vinegar is much more acidic than its Chinese counterpart, so start with very little and add slowly.
* Add or remove mushrooms, bamboo shoots, or tofu as needed. These three ingredients don't add much to the taste, mostly they add to the texture of the soup.

'''Lime and mascarpone cheesecake''' is a very creamy and delightfully simple dessert. It can be prepared ahead of time and stored in the fridge. No cooking is required.

==Procedure==
#Melt the butter in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and add the biscuit crumbs. Press firmly into a 20 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] diameter loose-bottomed pan and put aside.

'''Eton mess''' is a [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] of English origin consisting of a mixture of strawberries, pieces of meringue and cream, which is traditionally served at Eton College's annual prize-giving celebration picnic on the "Fourth of June" (actually celebrated on the last Wednesday in May).<ref>{{cite web|title=Glossary C–G|url=http://www.joyofbaking.com/other/glossaryCG.html|publisher=JoyofBaking.com|accessdate=[[w:10 July|10 July]] [[w:2007|2007]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dates of Halves|url=http://www.etoncollege.com/Eton.asp?state=load&di=171|publisher=[[w:Eton College|Eton College]]|accessdate=[[w:6 December|6 December]] [[w:2007|2007]]}} {{cite web|title=Eton Glossary|url=http://www.etoncollege.com/eton.asp?di=321#fourthofjune|publisher=[[w:Eton College|Eton College]]|accessdate=[[w:6 December|6 December]] [[w:2007|2007]]}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
*4 medium-sized [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringues]]
*280 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 ⅕ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 9 ½ [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook:Cream|double cream]]
*50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Icing sugar|icing sugar]]
*10 ml (1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla essence]]
*150 ml (⅗ cup or 5 fl oz) Greek [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]
*500 g (2 ⅕ cups or 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] 2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]]

== Procedure ==
#Rinse the strawberries, remove the tops, and cut into halves.
#Break the meringues into pieces (not too small) and place into a bowl.
#Put the double cream, vanilla essence, and icing sugar into a bowl. [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] until reasonably stiff. 
#Combine the whipped cream, yoghurt, strawberries, and meringue, being careful not to mash the meringue into pieces that are too small.
#Serve in bowls.

recipes.title: Manhattan Clam Chowder I
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Clam recipes
| servings = 6
| time = 90 minutes
| difficulty = 1
| Image = [[Image:ManhattanClamChowder.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

'''Manhattan clam chowder''' is a [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] traditionally made from clams, herbs, tomatoes, and other vegetables. Despite its name, it originated in Rhode Island, not Manhattan.
 
Clam chowder, in its cream-based, [[Cookbook:New England Clam Chowder|New England version]], has existed since the mid-18th Century, and no mention of any Manhattan chowder has been found that predates the 1930s.{{fact}} Many restaurants in northern Rhode Island sell both red and white chowders, while the US southern coast favors clear and white chowders. Often they are served alongside clam cakes.

According to Alton Brown, who pointed this out in the installment of his program ''Good Eats'' titled "Send In The Clams," the use of tomatoes instead of milk was initially the work of Portuguese immigrants in Rhode Island, as tomato-based stews were already a traditional part of Portuguese cuisine. New Englanders called this modified version Manhattan-style clam chowder as a pejorative because, in their snide view, calling someone a New Yorker was an insult.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Send in the Clams |url=https://www.foodnetwork.com/shows/good-eats/episodes/send-in-the-clams |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Food Network |language=en}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (425 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) canned [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], or 2 small boiled potatoes
* 28 ounces (794 g) canned [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] in juice, or 2 large tomatoes and tomato juice
* 6.5 ounces (184 g) canned [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Clam|clams]], minimum
* 2 stalks of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]

== Procedure ==
#Core the tomatoes. Remove the pale parts and the seeds; the "meat" of the tomato will be what will be used. For canned tomatoes, a strainer will be helpful.
#Chop all non-clam ingredients to match the clams in size.
#If desired add spices. Suggestions offered include [[Cookbook:Dill|dill seed]], [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Celery|celery seed]], [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]], [[Cookbook:Marjoram|marjoram]], and/or fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]. Alternatively, [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] can be used in lieu of the marjoram.
#Cook the chowder, without boiling, until the celery begins to soften.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* A sturdy type of [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] can be used in place of the clams; good choices include catfish, tilapia, and pollock. 
* Cooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] can be substituted for the potatoes, the celery can be replaced with [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] or [[Cookbook:Seaweed|seaweed]], and [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] can be added.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:North American cuisines|North American Cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ontario|Cuisine of Ontario]]

'''Sweet cornbread''' is a variant of the[[Cookbook:Skillet Cornbread | Skillet Cornbread]] made throughout central and eastern Ontario and Quebec and is sometimes known by the alternative name of Johnny Cake.<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia
  | title = Johnny-cake
  | encyclopedia = [[Oxford English Dictionary]]
  | volume =
  | pages =
  | publisher =
  | year = 1989
  | id =
  | accessdate = 14 March 2010}}</ref> Its presence in these southern regions of Canada is thought to be due to the influx of British Loyalists from what is now the Southern United States moving to the then-English-controlled colonies during the American War of Independence.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (140 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[cookbook:cornmeal|cornmeal]]
* 2 cups (275 g / 9.7 oz) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ½ cup (160 g / 5.6 oz) [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]]
* ½ cup (90 g / 3.2 oz) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* ½ cup (125 g / 4.4 oz) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

== Procedure ==

# In a large bowl beat eggs lightly to break the yolks as one would for scrambled eggs, then mix in the butter. Soften the butter beforehand if you must by heating it a little.
# The butter/egg mixture should be loose. Add the sugar and maple syrup, mix well, then add the salt to the liquid mixture.
# Mix the cornmeal and baking powder, then blend them into the liquids.
# Slowly add the flour as needed to reach a proper cake [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] texture. This should be softer than a cookie [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]], able to stick to the mixing spoon and come off in blobs. You may not need all of the flour, or may even need a little more based on your eggs and how closely you measured.
# Pour into a greased pan, put into an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] heated to 200°C (400°F), and let [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for between 15–25 minutes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When mixing the batter, be sure it is soft enough for a typical cake; you do not want it too moist or dry. Use milk to fill in liquid you need and a half-and-half mix of flour and cornmeal if you are too moist.

* Keep a close eye on the cake while it bakes: it will become hard fast if you do not take it out in time.

* If you want to make a crisper crust take a 3 part mix of equal volumes of flour, cornmeal and brown sugar, mix well. Add to the top of the cake half way into the baking process, but do this very quickly: leaving the door open too long will make your cake a rock.  The amount required varies based on the pan you use, so use your eyes for what you need (less than a cup total).  Despite the call for opening it halfway through baking, adding it at the beginning should work fine as well.

* You can substitute honey for the maple syrup, or plain sugar. Maple is used for its flavouring as much as its sweetness.

* Margarine or vegetable oil will do as well as butter for this. Butter was used traditionally and is thus listed.

* This dish is usually made for after meals and outside them rather than with them, which is how its cousin [[Cookbook:Skillet Cornbread | Skillet Cornbread]] is used.  However, when having [[Cookbook:Maple Beans | Maple Beans]] and Ham, Sweet Cornbread is often served with it.

recipes.title: Asparagus Soup
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Soup recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

== Ingredients ==
*12 thick [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]] spears
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water
*1 medium [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*¼–1 cup whipping or light [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], and [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]] to taste

== Procedure ==
#Snap the tough ends off the asparagus spears. 
#Bring the water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in a medium [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], salt the water lightly, and add the asparagus spears. Cook at a lively simmer for 10 minutes.  Lift out with [[Cookbook:Tongs|tongs]] and set aside. Reserve the cooking water.
#In a separate saucepan large enough to hold the finished soup, heat the butter, add the chopped shallot, and cook gently until soft but not browned. Add the cooked asparagus spears and one cup of the cooking water and bring to a boil. Cook at a lively simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain the soup through a medium [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] into a bowl, reserving the liquid. 
#Purée the solids in a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] with enough of the reserved liquid to allow the mixture to purée smoothly.
#Strain the purée through the sieve back into the [[Cookbook:Non-reactive|non-reactive]] saucepan, rubbing the mixture through with a flexible scraper or wooden spoon and leaving the fibrous parts in the sieve. Discard the contents of the sieve.
#Add the cream and enough of the remaining asparagus cooking water to give the soup the consistency you want. Season to taste with salt, freshly ground black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Reheat gently over low heat, making sure not to let the soup boil.
#Serve hot or chilled. If you want to serve it chilled, let it cool, then refrigerate it uncovered until thoroughly cold, then cover with [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|plastic wrap]]. You can keep it refrigerated for up to 2 days.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Don't be tempted to omit the final straining of the soup! If you leave the bits of fibrous asparagus skin in the soup, they give it a very unpleasant texture. Use a sieve with a medium mesh, not too coarse and not too fine: too coarse will let too much of the fiber through, too fine will make the job of straining too difficult.
*The richest version of this recipe, using a full cup of whipping cream, produces an especially luscious and velvety soup. For a lighter soup with fewer calories, use the smaller amount of whipping cream or substitute light cream. If you're planning to use only ¼ cup of cream, cook the asparagus in 3 cups of water so that you'll have enough cooking water to add to the finished soup to achieve the right consistency.
*To make this soup vegan, cook the asparagus in 3 cups of water, omit the cream, and use oil instead of butter to cook the shallot. 

[[Category:Recipes using asparagus|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes for soup|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Vegetarian recipes]]

[[Category:Recipes using cayenne]]
[[Category:Recipes using whipping cream]]
[[Category:Recipes using light cream]]
ingredients_original: ¼–1 cup whipping or light cream
Salt, freshly ground black pepper, and cayenne pepper to taste
steps_original: Snap the tough ends off the asparagus spears.

Bring the water to a boil in a medium saucepan, salt the water lightly, and add the asparagus spears. Cook at a lively simmer for 10 minutes. Lift out with tongs and set aside. Reserve the cooking water.

In a separate saucepan large enough to hold the finished soup, heat the butter, add the chopped shallot, and cook gently until soft but not browned. Add the cooked asparagus spears and one cup of the cooking water and bring to a boil. Cook at a lively simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain the soup through a medium sieve into a bowl, reserving the liquid.
Purée the solids in a food processor with enough of the reserved liquid to allow the mixture to purée smoothly.

Strain the purée through the sieve back into the non-reactive saucepan, rubbing the mixture through with a flexible scraper or wooden spoon and leaving the fibrous parts in the sieve. Discard the contents of the sieve.

Add the cream and enough of the remaining asparagus cooking water to give the soup the consistency you want. Season to taste with salt, freshly ground black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Reheat gently over low heat, making sure not to let the soup boil.
Serve hot or chilled. If you want to serve it chilled, let it cool, then refrigerate it uncovered until thoroughly cold, then cover with plastic wrap. You can keep it refrigerated for up to 2 days.

*Don't be tempted to omit the final straining of the soup! If you leave the bits of fibrous asparagus skin in the soup, they give it a very unpleasant texture. Use a sieve with a medium mesh, not too coarse and not too fine: too coarse will let too much of the fiber through, too fine will make the job of straining too difficult.
*The richest version of this recipe, using a full cup of whipping cream, produces an especially luscious and velvety soup. For a lighter soup with fewer calories, use the smaller amount of whipping cream or substitute light cream. If you're planning to use only ¼ cup of cream, cook the asparagus in 3 cups of water so that you'll have enough cooking water to add to the finished soup to achieve the right consistency.
*To make this soup vegan, cook the asparagus in 3 cups of water, omit the cream, and use oil instead of butter to cook the shallot.

'''Yerushalmi kugel''' is named after the city of Jerusalem. Legend has it that it originated in Jerusalem with the followers of the Vilna Gaon in the 18th century.

==Ingredients==
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]] ([[Cookbook:Egg noodles|egg noodles]] are preferred, but others work fine as well)

*1 handful of [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] noodles according to the package instructions and drain.
#Heat the olive oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]], and add ⅓ cup (80 g) sugar.
#Stir continuously until the sugar begins to brown. Remove from heat.
#The sugar will continue to brown for a few more minutes, creating a thick caramel.
#Add the caramel to the noodles.
#Add the sugar, eggs, cinnamon, pepper, and raisins. Stir.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a pan at 350°F (180°C) until the top begins to brown (about 40 minutes).

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan, and add ⅓ cup (80 g) sugar.

recipes.title: Risotto II
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Rice recipes|servings=6|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]

This is a traditional Italian '''risotto'''.

==Ingredients==

* 5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]]
* 2½ [[Cookbook:cup|cups]] risotto [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Wine|white wine]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Broth|chicken broth]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Saffron|saffron powder]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

==Procedure==
# Bring the stock to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Keep the temperature as high as possible throughout the cooking process, without letting the stock [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. The surface of the stock should just be moving a little. 
# [[Cookbook:Sauté|Sauté]] the onion until soft.
# Add the rice and mix well until it is coated the oil.
# Add the wine and stir constantly over medium heat until it evaporates.
# Add enough hot broth to cover the rice and continue to stir until the liquid is absorbed.
# Keep adding hot broth, a little at a time, while constantly stirring until the rice is done.
# In a small bowl, dissolve the saffron in a little hot broth and add it to the rice.
# Stir in the Parmesan cheese and season with salt to taste.
# Serve immediately.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Plump, medium-grain rice that contains a lot of starch is required. Arborio or Carnaroli types are traditionally best. Other rices that work well are Roma, Vialone, Nano, and Maratelli.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] 
==Ingredients==

* 1 stick [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 cup white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 5 fresh [[Cookbook:Peach|peaches]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|375°F]].
# Melt margarine in [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] size [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|baking pan]] or dish. Set aside.
# Mix baking powder, flour, sugar, and milk. Pour this batter over the melted margarine, and do not stir.
# Arrange peaches over the batter.
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] 20–30 minutes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If camping, or if fresh peaches are not in season, you can use a #2 (half-size) can of sliced peaches, drained.
* If using a [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]], preheat with about 15 charcoal briquettes, with 10 or 11 on the top and 4 or 5 on the bottom (for the 12-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] size).
* If possible use a 1.5-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] deep, 1.5–2-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] baking dish.

A '''cherry''' '''soda''' is a soda flavored with cherries. 

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) water
* 20 frozen pitted [[Cookbook:Cherry|cherries]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]], as needed

== Procedure ==

# Combine the water, cherries, and sugar in a pot.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the mixture until it becomes a thick syrup.
# [[Cookbook:Sieve|Strain]] the mixture, and discard the solids. This should yield about 5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (150 ml) syrup.
# To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

'''Hot pineapple side dish''' is a casserole of pineapple with cheese.

* 1 can (20 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] / 600 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple chunks]]

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| Category = Tofu recipes
| Servings = 6–8
| Time = 60 minutes
| Difficulty = 3
| Rating = 3
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Tofu|Tofu]]

== Ingredients ==

* 6–8 whole [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom pods]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] whole [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander seeds]]
* ½ tsp whole [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin seeds]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]

*4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*1–2 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] coarsely
*1 extra-firm or firm [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] block, cut into ¾-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] cubes
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Currant|currants]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
*½ cup 2% plain [[Cookbook:yogurt|yogurt]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (optional)
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] (optional)
*¼ cup (or more) [[Cookbook:Almond|slivered almonds]], lightly toasted
*⅛ cup toasted [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] threads or flakes (optional)

==Procedure==
# Crack open the cardamom pods. Reserve the seeds; discard the shells.
# Heat oil to quite hot but not smoking in a [[Cookbook:Skillet|pan]]. Add spices and bay leaf. Cook until seeds crack (1–2 minutes).
# Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and garlic, then cook until tender and translucent.
# Reserve onion, garlic, spices to a side dish.
# Season tofu with salt and pepper. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]], adding oil if needed. When tofu is heated through, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until lightly brown (5–8 minutes).
# Add reserved onion/spice mixture.
# Add currants and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] for 3–5 minutes. At this point, the tofu may be cooled and chilled for re-heating the following day.
# Add sour cream, yogurt, coconut milk, and butter. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until sauce has cooked down a little.
# Add toasted almonds and toasted coconut.
# Serve hot with [[Cookbook:Saffron Sweet Rice|Saffron Sweet Rice]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When reheated, this dish tastes as well as, or better than, when freshly cooked!

recipes.title: Fried Bananas
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Recipes for dessert
| servings = 4
| time = About 20 minutes
| difficulty = 2
| Energy = About 150–200 Cal per serving
| Image = [[File:Pisang goreng (fried bananas).jpg|300px|Fried Bananas]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Recipes for dessert]]

'''Fried bananas''' is a delightful [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] or snack enjoyed in many cuisines around the world. These sweet, caramelized banana slices offer a perfect balance of crispy and tender textures. Whether served on their own or as a topping for ice cream or pancakes, fried bananas are a simple yet satisfying treat.

== Ingredients ==
* 4 ripe [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
* Vanilla [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]] (optional, for serving)

== Procedure ==

# Heat a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet or frying pan]] over medium heat and melt the butter.
# Add the banana slices to the pan and sprinkle them with brown sugar.
# Cook the bananas for 2–3 minutes on each side or until they turn golden brown and caramelized.
# If desired, sprinkle cinnamon over the bananas during cooking.
# Remove the fried bananas from the pan and serve them hot. Optionally, serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream for an extra treat.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Experiment with different spices like nutmeg for unique flavour variations.
* Drizzle honey or chocolate syrup over the fried bananas for added sweetness.
* You can also add a splash of rum or liqueur for an adult twist on this dessert.
* Fried bananas can be served as a topping for pancakes, waffles, or French toast.
* See [[Cookbook:Kele Ka Halwa (Fried Bananas in Milk)|kele ka halwa]] and [[Cookbook:Jamaican Banana Fritters|Jamaican banana fritters]] for similar dishes.

recipes.title: Risengrød
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Pudding recipes | Servings = 2 | Time = '''Total:''' 45 minutes
'''Prep:''' 5 minutes
'''Cooking:''' 40 minutes | Difficulty = 1 }}{{Recipe}} '''Risengrød''' is part of the Nordic Christmas tradition as a dinner dish. It is simply rice boiled with milk and a little sugar to form porridge, and it is served warm with butter and cinnamon-sugar.{{Cite web |title=Risengrød {{!}} Public Domain Recipes |url=https://publicdomainrecipes.com/risengroed/ |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=publicdomainrecipes.com}} ==Ingredients== *3 [[Cookbook:dl|dl]] (300 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] / 1¼ [[Cookbook:cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:water|water]] *180 [[Cookbook:g|g]] porridge [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] *1 [[Cookbook:liter|liter]] whole [[Cookbook:milk|milk]] *2 [[Cookbook:pinch|pinches]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]] *4 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tbsp]] white granulated [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]] *2 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:cinnamon|cinnamon]] *50 g [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] ==Equipment== *[[Cookbook:Stock Pot|Deep pot]] with lid *[[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Bowl]] *Mixing spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] ==Procedure== # Bring water and rice to a [[Cookbook:boiling|boil]] in a deep pot. Boil the rice at steady heat and with active stirring for approximately 2 minutes. # Add milk and return to a boil. Simmer over low heat, stirring actively for approximately 10 minutes. # Put on lid and simmer for approximately 30 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking. # Test the porridge for thickness—if it seems too thin, simmer for another 5–10 minutes. # Add salt. # Combine sugar and cinnamon in a bowl or container. # Serve porridge warm with cinnamon-sugar on top and a bit of butter in the middle. ==References== [[Category:Recipes using white sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using rice]] [[Category:Recipes using butter]] [[Category:Recipes using whole milk]] [[Category:Recipes for rice pudding]] [[Category:Danish recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using cinnamon]] [[Category:Christmas recipes]]
steps_original: Bring water and rice to a boil in a deep pot. Boil the rice at steady heat and with active stirring for approximately 2 minutes.
Add milk and return to a boil. Simmer over low heat, stirring actively for approximately 10 minutes.
Put on lid and simmer for approximately 30 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking.
Test the porridge for thickness—if it seems too thin, simmer for another 5–10 minutes.
Add salt.
Combine sugar and cinnamon in a bowl or container.
Serve porridge warm with cinnamon-sugar on top and a bit of butter in the middle.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Peanut Butter Toast
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Breakfast recipes|servings=1|time=7 minutes|difficulty=1}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

You've heard of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, and you've heard of peanut butter toast. Why not combine them!?

==Ingredients==

* 1 slice of [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* 2–4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]], smooth or crunchy
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]

==Procedure==

# [[cookbook:toast|Toast]] the bread on both sides in a [[Cookbook:Oven|toaster oven]], using the broiler setting.
# Smear the peanut butter on the bread.
# Sprinkle chocolate chips lightly (or heavily, if you want!) over the peanut butter.
# Put the toast back under the broiler for about 20 seconds to melt the chocolate.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some people like to spread the chocolate chips, after softening under the broiler.
* One variation is to spread marshmallow fluff over the peanut butter, replace the chocolate chips with a Nestles' crunch bar, use 2 toasts, and make it a sandwich.
* Instead of heating the chocolate under the broiler, add cold chocolate chips (from the refrigerator) for a nice temperature contrast.
* According to taste, use milk, dark, semisweet, or white chocolate chips.

recipes.title: Drover's Damper
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Bread recipes|servings=5–10|time=50 minutes|difficulty=3
}}[[Image:Mustering camp.jpg|250px|thumb|Damper and camp oven used, Walcha, NSW]]{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Australia|Australian Cuisine]] 

'''Drover's damper''' is Australian bread, made by stockmen while taking care of or rounding up stock. It is meant to be made outside by a campfire. This is the "flash" version, made when butter and milk are available.

==Ingredients==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[cookbook:Flour|self-raising flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 2 teaspoons [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 1 cup [[cookbook:milk|milk]]

==Procedure==

# Add salt to flour, then add sugar.
# Rub in butter.
# [[cookbook:Mix|Mix]] in milk to make a medium-soft [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[cookbook:Knead|Knead]] lightly on flat surface until smooth.
# Pat dough into a round shape.
# Place damper mixture on coals or hot ash. Cook for maximum of 40 minutes.
# Discard burnt outside and eat the inside.
# Serve with [[cookbook:butter|butter]], ([[cookbook:Golden Syrup|golden syrup]]) or [[cookbook:jam|jam]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* This cookbook also has an [[Cookbook:Damper|"ordinary" damper]] recipe.
* You can do this using a hole near the fire in a greased [[cookbook:dutch oven|camp oven]] or greased [[cookbook:aluminium foil|aluminium foil]] in a barbecue.
* If you aren't outdoors, just add mixture to greased bread tin, [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] with [[cookbook:milk|milk]] and cook in a hot [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], reducing heat until cooked (20 minutes).
* You can add dried [[cookbook:fruit|fruit]] to make "[[cookbook:Johnny Cake|Johnny Cake]]".
* As a variation, add grated [[cookbook:cheese|cheese]].
* Use [[cookbook:beer|beer]] instead of milk to make "Beer Damper".

==External links==
*[http://www.nla.gov.au/ntwkpubs/gw/49/p09a01.html Drovers Oral History Project ]  National Library of Australia
*[http://www.australianoutdoors.com/damper.htm Australian Bush Damper ] Gerry & Mo Noterey from Australian Outdoors (Variation recipes with pictures!)

recipes.title: Indian Butter Chicken I
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
|Category = Indian recipes
|Servings = 4 to 6
|Image = [[Image:Butter_Chicken_with_Naan.JPG|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]]

'''Butter chicken''' or '''murgh makhani''' is an [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] dish popular in countries all over the world where Indian restaurants are found. The dish was invented by accident at Moti Mahal Restaurant in Daryaganj, New Delhi. While the dish's general recipe is well known, the actual flavor can vary from restaurant to restaurant even within Delhi.

The dish is made by [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinating]] chicken overnight in a yoghurt and [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spice]] mixture. The chicken is then roasted or baked.

A sauce is made from butter, tomatoes, [[cookbook:almond|almond]]s and various spices, usually including the famous tandoori masala spice mix, and sometimes cream. Once the sauce is prepared, the marinated and roasted chicken is chopped and added to it.

{{see also|Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala}}

==Ingredients==

*400–500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] of skinless, boneless [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] thighs or breasts (with the bone, this will probably be 800 g)
*50 g [[Cookbook:Tandoori masala|tandoori masala]] powder
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of unsweetened [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]
*1 small [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] or [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]], juiced
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] finely
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
*2–3 cloves of crushed [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
*2 teaspoons of grated [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
*1 tablespoon of ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
*2–3 teaspoons of [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder
*100–200 g [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*100 g [[Cookbook:Cream|full cream]]
==Procedure==
# Trim and cut the chicken into small cubes. If you prefer chicken on the bone, cut long thin slices laterally into the chicken.
# In a big bowl combine the tandoori powder, yogurt, lemon juice, and chicken. Massage this well with your hands so that all the chicken is evenly covered in the Tandoori powder. Cover and put aside for at least ½ an hour.
# Heat a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] until evenly hot.  
# In the pan melt 2 tablespoons of butter until it is frothy. Add the onions and the cinnamon to the pan and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] lightly. When the onions are soft and starting to brown, stir in the crushed garlic and ginger. Then add the turmeric, chili, and coriander, and sauté over a medium heat.  
# Add the chicken and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]], stirring constantly until the chicken has turned white. This doesn't take long, so make sure you don't overcook the chicken.
# Mix in the tomato paste. Add the cream and heat through. After adding the cream and stirring, you may add additional tandoori masala. About 3–5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] is generally sufficient.
# Cover and simmer for just over 10 minutes.

[[Category:Recipes using chicken]]
[[Category:Gluten-free recipes]]
[[Category:Recipes_with_metric_units]]
[[Category:Recipes using butter]]
[[Category:Recipes using chile]]
[[Category:Recipes using ground cinnamon]]
[[Category:Recipes using lime juice]]
[[Category:Recipes using lemon juice]]
[[Category:Recipes using coriander]]
[[Category:Recipes using garlic]]
[[Category:Recipes using fresh ginger]]
ingredients_original: 400–500 g of skinless, boneless chicken thighs or breasts (with the bone, this will probably be 800 g)
steps_original: Trim and cut the chicken into small cubes. If you prefer chicken on the bone, cut long thin slices laterally into the chicken.

In a big bowl combine the tandoori powder, yogurt, lemon juice, and chicken. Massage this well with your hands so that all the chicken is evenly covered in the Tandoori powder. Cover and put aside for at least ½ an hour.
Heat a large saucepan or frying pan until evenly hot.

In the pan melt 2 tablespoons of butter until it is frothy. Add the onions and the cinnamon to the pan and fry lightly. When the onions are soft and starting to brown, stir in the crushed garlic and ginger. Then add the turmeric, chili, and coriander, and sauté over a medium heat.
Add the chicken and sauté, stirring constantly until the chicken has turned white. This doesn't take long, so make sure you don't overcook the chicken.
Mix in the tomato paste. Add the cream and heat through. After adding the cream and stirring, you may add additional tandoori masala. About 3–5 tablespoons is generally sufficient.
Cover and simmer for just over 10 minutes.

recipes.original_wikitext:
__notoc__
{{Recipe}}

{{recipesummary

| Servings = 4
| Time = 25 hours

| Rating = 
}}An '''energy drink''' is a heavily caffeinated soft drink. This recipe contains a lot of caffeine and citrus. This recipe has been modified from a discussion at Stack Exchange.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How can I replicate the flavor of Mountain Dew? |url=https://cooking.stackexchange.com/questions/65160/how-can-i-replicate-the-flavor-of-mountain-dew |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Seasoned Advice |language=en}}</ref> 

Note that consuming high levels of caffeine can be very dangerous. If you are scaling the recipe up or down, make sure you scale the caffeine accordingly so that the per-serving caffeine amount stays the same or is lower. Absolutely do not use more than the listed proportion of caffeine; this will result in hospitalization or even death. 
== Ingredients ==

* ½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], zested in strips and juiced
* ½ ea. [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]], zested in strips and juiced
* ½ ea. [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]], zested in strips and juiced
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:White sugar|white sugar]]
* 30 mg [[Cookbook:Caffeine|caffeine]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]], as needed

== Procedure ==

# Combine the citrus zests and sugar, rubbing the sugar into the peels to extract the oils. Let this mixture rest in the fridge for 24 hours to infuse.
# Combine the sugar-zest mixture with the citrus juices and caffeine. Stir well to dissolve the sugar and get a [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]].
# [[Cookbook:Sieve|Strain]] the syrup—this should yield approximately 5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (150 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) syrup.
# To make the finished beverage, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

recipes.original_wikitext:
[[Category:Recipes using rice flour]][[Category:Recipes using rice flour]]{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=15 minutes, plus 1 hour baking|difficulty=1
| Image = [[Image:Crumble à la rhubarbe.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|Rhubarb]]

'''Rhubarb crumble''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|British]] [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]]. Served traditionally with [[Cookbook:Custard|custard]] (though you can of course serve with [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or [[Cookbook:Vanilla Ice Cream|ice cream]]) it is a hearty, filling, and warm feast, best served after a light meal. This version has a flour-based crumble topping, it and simply uses rhubarb and sugar as the filling (unlike the cornstarch etc. in other versions). The rhubarb juice acts as a sufficient sauce.

== Ingredients ==
*400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1 ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|rhubarb]], cut into pieces roughly 1.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] long (no need to be consistent)
*15 g (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) light [[Cookbook:Sugar|brown sugar]]
*75 g (2 ½ [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], cut in pieces
*100 g (3 ½ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|wholemeal flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°C (180°C fan).
#Rinse and drain the rhubarb pieces, and place them in a deep [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|ovenproof dish]]. Add the light brown sugar and mix briefly.
#Put the flours in a mixing bowl. Add the butter. With your fingers (not the palms of your hands), rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
#Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon over this mixture, and mix them in briefly.
#Sprinkle the crumble mixture over the fruit, making a complete layer. Do not press the topping down—you want it light and crumbly.
#Put the dish in the oven (no lid) for 35–45 minutes until crisp and a bit brown.
#Serve with custard.

steps_original: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Rinse and drain the rhubarb pieces, and place them in a deep ovenproof dish. Add the light brown sugar and mix briefly.
Put the flours in a mixing bowl. Add the butter. With your fingers (not the palms of your hands), rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon over this mixture, and mix them in briefly.
Sprinkle the crumble mixture over the fruit, making a complete layer. Do not press the topping down—you want it light and crumbly.
Put the dish in the oven (no lid) for 35–45 minutes until crisp and a bit brown.
Serve with custard.

recipes.title: Corn Bread Fish
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Fish recipes|servings=4|time=⅛ hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southern cuisine|Southern cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]] 

==Ingredients==

* 4 boneless, skinless [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] fillets (about 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] each, 1–1¼ [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] at thickest), such as [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]], [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]] or [[Cookbook:Trout|trout]] (see notes)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] bottled [[Cookbook:Italian Dressing|Italian dressing]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|corn muffin]], or ⅔ cup coarse crumbs
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], or 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] lemon juice

==Procedure==

# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]] (204°C).
# Spray a glass [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] with [[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|cooking-oil spray]].
# Season each fish piece with salt and pepper, and place in the dish.
# Pour the dressing evenly over the fish.
# Crumble the corn muffin, and sprinkle the crumbs over the fish.
# Place the dish in the preheated oven, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] until the dressing is bubbling at the edges, the crumbs lightly brown, and the thickest part of the fillets are opaque and flake easily with a fork (about 15 to 20 minutes).
# While fish is baking, cut the lemon into 4 parts and set aside.
# When the fish is done, remove it from the oven, squeeze the juice from the lemon quarters over the fish, and serve immediately.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If the only available fillets are large, cut two of them in half to make four servings.
* When placing the fish in the baking dish, the thick parts should not be layered.

Place the dish in the preheated oven, and bake until the dressing is bubbling at the edges, the crumbs lightly brown, and the thickest part of the fillets are opaque and flake easily with a fork (about 15 to 20 minutes).
While fish is baking, cut the lemon into 4 parts and set aside.
When the fish is done, remove it from the oven, squeeze the juice from the lemon quarters over the fish, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Shortbread
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Cookie recipes|servings=12|time=50 minutes|difficulty=2
| Image = [[Image:Shortbread fingers.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]
[[Image:Shortbreadrounds.jpg|thumb|Shortbread rounds before being baked|308x308px]]

'''Shortbread''' is a type of [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookie]] which is traditionally made from one part [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]], two parts [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], and three parts [[Cookbook:Flour|plain white flour]], although other ingredients like [[Cookbook:Rice flour|ground rice]] or [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] are sometimes added to alter the texture.  Shortbread is so named because of its crumbly texture (from an old meaning of the word short).  The cause of this texture is its high [[Cookbook:Fat|fat]] content, provided by the butter.  The related word "[[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]]" refers to any fat that may be added to produce a short (crumbly) texture.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.etymonline.com/index.php?term=shortening|accessdate=2007-01-25|title=Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

==Ingredients==
* 380 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 13 ½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 220 g (1 cup / 8 oz) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 110 g (½ cup / 4 oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]

==Equipment==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|wooden spoon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Fork|table fork]] (optional, leave out for Iced Shortbread)
* 1 scone cutter or circular [[Cookbook:Cookie Cutter|cookie cutter]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cooling rack|cooling rack]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|140°C (275°F or Gas Mark 1)]].
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] the butter with the sugar until light and fluffy.
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour and salt into the mixture and work into the fat and sugar until completely amalgamated.
#Shape the dough into a ball and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] to about 1.3 [[Cookbook:Centimetre|cm]] (½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) thick. The dough may need to be chilled for 10–15 minutes for easier handling.
#Cut into squares or rectangles and prick the tops with a fork in two parallel lines.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven for 30–40 minutes or until the shortbread is lightly browned.
#Leave them on a cooling rack to cool.
#Store in a cool place in an airtight container.

== Notes & Variations ==

* Some recipes call for a 1-2-3 ratio of sugar, fat, and flour, but fat is often increased to prevent dryness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kathrin |date=2022-11-10 |title=Schnelle 3-Zutaten-Kekse |url=https://www.backenmachtgluecklich.de/rezepte/einfache-kekse-aus-3-zutaten.html |access-date=2025-04-27 |website=Backen macht glücklich |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Myacooks |title=Real English Shortbread or 123 Shortbread Recipe - Food.com |url=https://www.food.com/recipe/real-english-shortbread-or-123-shortbread-442664 |access-date=2025-04-27 |website=www.food.com |language=en}}</ref>

==References==
<references/>

ingredients_original: 380 g (1 ½ cup / 13 ½ oz) all-purpose flour
110 g (½ cup / 4 oz) white granulated sugar
steps_original: Preheat the oven to 140°C (275°F or Gas Mark 1).
Cream the butter with the sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift the flour and salt into the mixture and work into the fat and sugar until completely amalgamated.
Shape the dough into a ball and roll out to about 1.3 cm (½ inch) thick. The dough may need to be chilled for 10–15 minutes for easier handling.
Cut into squares or rectangles and prick the tops with a fork in two parallel lines.
Bake in the oven for 30–40 minutes or until the shortbread is lightly browned.
Leave them on a cooling rack to cool.
Store in a cool place in an airtight container.

recipes.title: American Marinara Sauce I
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| category = Sauce recipes
| servings = 4 servings
| time = 30 minutes + 24 hours
| difficulty = 2
}}{{Recipe}}

This is the classic expensive restaurant edition. You only live once.

== Ingredients ==

* ½ stick unsalted sweet cream [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] vegetable or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 2 medium cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], crushed and chopped fine
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (80 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Red onion|red onion]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* ½ tsp dried crushed [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]]
* 1 can (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 750 g) unsalted whole peeled [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], reserve juice
* 1 can (6 oz / 150 g) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (more or less to taste)
* 1 ½ tsp granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]

== Procedure ==

# Heat a large [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]] over medium heat until hot (approximately 5 minutes).
# Add butter and oil; heat until clear and the bubbling stops.
# Add onion; gently [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] for 1 minute.
# Reduce heat to medium-low.
# Add garlic; gently sauté for 1 minute.
# Add tomato juice.
# Add tomatoes, one at a time, crushing completely using your hands (watch for spurts).
# Add oregano and red pepper flakes. Stir to combine.
# Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
# Add 1 tsp salt and sugar, black pepper, and tomato paste; Stir until paste is incorporated.
# Cover and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 10 minutes
# Taste and season accordingly. You do not want the sauce to be salty, just not unsalty. You do not want the sauce to be sweet, just not sour. Season by adding the remaining salt and sugar a little at a time, stirring completely between tastes.
# Serve over ''[[Cookbook:Al Dente|al dente]]'' spaghetti with a side of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] or [[Cookbook:Meatballs|meatballs]] and a deep sweet [[Cookbook:Red Wine|red wine]]; serves 4, make this for two and enjoy again tomorrow night!

[[Category:Italian recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes for pasta sauce|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes using tomato|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes for marinara sauce|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes using butter]]
[[Category:Recipes using granulated sugar]]
[[Category:Recipes using chile flake]]
ingredients_original: ½ stick unsalted sweet cream butter
2 medium cloves garlic, crushed and chopped fine
⅓ cup (80 g) diced red onion
½ tsp dried crushed red pepper flakes
1 can (28 oz / 750 g) unsalted whole peeled tomatoes, reserve juice
1 ½ tsp salt (more or less to taste)
steps_original: Heat a large pot over medium heat until hot (approximately 5 minutes).
Add butter and oil; heat until clear and the bubbling stops.
Add onion; gently sauté for 1 minute.
Reduce heat to medium-low.
Add garlic; gently sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomato juice.
Add tomatoes, one at a time, crushing completely using your hands (watch for spurts).
Add oregano and red pepper flakes. Stir to combine.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Add 1 tsp salt and sugar, black pepper, and tomato paste; Stir until paste is incorporated.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes

Taste and season accordingly. You do not want the sauce to be salty, just not unsalty. You do not want the sauce to be sweet, just not sour. Season by adding the remaining salt and sugar a little at a time, stirring completely between tastes.
Serve over al dente spaghetti with a side of Italian sausage or meatballs and a deep sweet red wine; serves 4, make this for two and enjoy again tomorrow night!

recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Soup|Soup recipes]]

'''Three sisters soup''' is a classic Indigenous recipe steeped in the folklore of the three staples of Indigenous cultures in North America: corn, squash, and beans. This hearty and delicious [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] pays homage to the rich heritage and agricultural traditions of Indigenous communities. It is wonderful on its own or served with freshly baked Indigenous bread.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] drained canned white or yellow hominy [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]] (can be substituted with regular corn)
* 2 cups trimmed and snapped fresh [[Cookbook:Green_beans|green beans]]
* 2 cups peeled and [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]] [[Cookbook:Butternut Squash|butternut squash]]
* 1½ cups white or yellow [[Cookbook:Potatoes|potatoes]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] (for a sweeter variation, you can use [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]])
* 5 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|chicken bouillon granules]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==

# In a large pot, combine the hominy, green beans, squash, and potatoes.
# Add water and chicken bouillon.
# Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce heat to low and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until the vegetables are soft (approximately 10 minutes).
# In a separate pan, melt the butter and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] in the flour. Stir the mixture into the soup.
# Increase heat to medium and cook until the soup thickens (approximately 5 minutes).
# Season with salt and pepper to taste.
# Serve your delicious three sisters soup. Garnish with fresh herbs or Indigenous spices for added flavor.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* To enhance the Indigenous flavors, consider using traditional Indigenous spices or herbs.
* Feel free to adjust the vegetable quantities to your preference.
* See [[Cookbook:Three Sisters Stew|Three Sisters Stew]] for another variation.

{{recipe}}

This salad is very easy to make. 

== Ingredients ==
* 1 pickling [[cookbook:cucumber|cucumber]]
* 1 large [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]]
* 1 head [[cookbook:onion|onion]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:vegetable oil|sunflower oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste

== Procedure ==
# [[cookbook:Chop|Chop]] cucumbers and tomatoes into small cubes (approx. ¼ inch on the side).
# Peel and chop the onion.
# Combine all of the above in an appropriately sized bowl.
# Add sunflower oil and mix well.
# Add salt to taste and mix again.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Sunflower oil is usually available at ethnic stores. If not available, it can be substituted for any vegetable oil, although that will change the authentic taste.
* A chopped [[cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]] or a couple can be optionally added to the mix for a "greener" taste.
* The salad should better be all used up at once; the taste starts to deteriorate after a few hours.

__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary|category=Cookie recipes|servings=25|time=Prep: 15 minutes
Baking: 20 minutes|difficulty=2|image=[[Image:Single ANZAC biscuit.jpg|300px]] }}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Australia|Cuisine of Australia]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of New Zealand|Cuisine of New Zealand]] '''ANZAC biscuits''' have long had an association with the Australia/New Zealand Army Corps ([[w:Australian and New Zealand Army Corps|ANZAC]]) troops sent to Gallipoli during WWI. The biscuit appears to be a variant of the Scottish oat cake, said to be from the Scottish-influenced city of Dunedin. The recipe was created to ensure the biscuits would keep well during naval transportation to loved ones who were fighting abroad. The finished biscuits are quite chewy and crisp, and have a long shelf-life. ==Ingredients== * 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] plain (non-self raising) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] * 1 cup white or brown [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * 2 cups rolled or instant [[Cookbook:Oats|oats]] * 1 cup desiccated [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] flakes * 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Golden Syrup|golden syrup]], [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]], or [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] * 225 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]] * 2 tablespoons of water ==Procedure== #Mix the flour, sugar, oats, and coconut in a bowl. #Melt the syrup and butter in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Add the baking soda and water to the syrup mix. #Mix the wet and dry ingredients, adding water if necessary. #Separate and roll the mixture into small balls, and flatten them on [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|oven trays]]. #[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 150°C (300°F) for about 20 minutes or until golden brown. ==Notes, tips, and variations== {{Wikipedia|Anzac biscuit}} * Using [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]] instead of [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]] gives more colour and flavour. * You can replace coconut with more syrup and oats. * Don't omit the baking soda and water. They give the biscuits crispness and colour. * See [https://www.awm.gov.au/articles/encyclopedia/anzac/biscuit/recipe https://www.awm.gov.au/articles/encyclopedia/anzac/biscuit/recipe] for the official ANZAC recipe. == See also == * [[Cookbook:Anzac Biscuits II|Anzac Biscuits II]] [[Category:New Zealand recipes]] [[Category:Australian recipes]] [[Category:Recipes for cookies]] [[Category:Recipes using oat]] [[Category:Vegetarian recipes]] [[Category:Baking recipes]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes with images]] [[Category:Recipes using butter]] [[Category:Recipes for dessert]] [[Category:Recipes using baking soda]] [[Category:Recipes using white sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using coconut]] [[Category:Recipes using corn syrup]] [[Category:Recipes using all-purpose flour]] [[Category:Recipes using golden syrup]] [[Category:Recipes using honey]] [[Category:Recipes using margarine]] [[Category:Recipes using brown sugar]]
ingredients_original: 4 tablespoons golden syrup, corn syrup, or honey
steps_original: Mix the flour, sugar, oats, and coconut in a bowl.
Melt the syrup and butter in a saucepan. Add the baking soda and water to the syrup mix.
Mix the wet and dry ingredients, adding water if necessary.
Separate and roll the mixture into small balls, and flatten them on oven trays.
Bake at 150°C (300°F) for about 20 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Pabellón Criollo (Venezuelan Rice and Beans with Steak)
recipes.source_title: Cookbook:Pabellón Criollo (Venezuelan Rice and Beans with Steak)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
|Category = Venezuelan recipes
|Servings = 4
|Time = 40 minutes
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Venezuela|Cuisine of Venezuela]]

'''Pabellón criollo''' is Venezuela's national dish, and no visit to this South American country will be complete unless you try it. This flavorful dish consists of shredded flank steak, black beans, rice, plantains or bananas, onions, tomatoes, and spices. The end result and presentation should resemble the national flag, hence the name of the dish. It is traditionally served with [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]], [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]] and [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]].

==Ingredients==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] finely chopped [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) tinned chopped [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 900 g (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|lean steak]], (sirloin or rump), about 12 mm (½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) thick

==Procedure==
# Heat the oil in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], add the onions and garlic and cook over a medium heat for about 5 minutes until the onions are soft and transparent.
# Add the tomatoes, cumin and salt, mix well, reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered, for about 30 minutes, stirring often, until the tomato juices evaporate and the sauce becomes thick. 
# 15 minutes before the end of the cooking time, preheat the [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] to hot, place the steak on the grill pan and cook under the grill for 5 minute on each side. 
# Remove from the grill and cut into pieces about 12mm/ ½-inch long and 6mm/ ¼-inch wide then add the strips of beef to the sauce, mixing well. 

[[Category:Venezuelan recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:Recipes using beef|{{PAGENAME}}]]
[[Category:South American recipes]]
[[Category:Recipes using garlic]]
[[Category:Recipes using onion]]
[[Category:Recipes using ground cumin]]
[[Category:Recipes using salt]]

steps_original: Heat the oil in a large saucepan, add the onions and garlic and cook over a medium heat for about 5 minutes until the onions are soft and transparent.
Add the tomatoes, cumin and salt, mix well, reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered, for about 30 minutes, stirring often, until the tomato juices evaporate and the sauce becomes thick.
15 minutes before the end of the cooking time, preheat the grill to hot, place the steak on the grill pan and cook under the grill for 5 minute on each side.
Remove from the grill and cut into pieces about 12mm/ ½-inch long and 6mm/ ¼-inch wide then add the strips of beef to the sauce, mixing well.
