recipes.title: Spaghetti with Bolognese Meat Sauce
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Italian recipes|servings=4|time=2 hours|difficulty=3
| Image = [[Image:Spaghetti Bolognese.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Cuisine of Italy]]

This northern Italian meat sauce, or Ragu Bolognese, is wonderful on [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] with freshly grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|Parmesan cheese]], or as filling for lasagne. 

==Ingredients==
*¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (125 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] or [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], cut into cubes
*1 lb (450 g) [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] lean or medium ground 
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (225 ml) coarsely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*¼ cup (50 ml) coarsely chopped [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
*¼ cup (50 ml) coarsely chopped [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
*¼ cup (50 ml) coarsely chopped [[Cookbook:Fennel|fennel]] bulb, if available
*¼ cup (50 ml) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] 
*1 cup (225 ml) canned plum [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]]
*½ cup (125 ml) red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
*2 cups (500 ml) beef [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] (preferably fresh, but canned beef stock will do)
*¼ cup (50 ml) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*1 strip of [[Cookbook:lemon rind|lemon rind]] 
*1 [[cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
*1 lb (450 g) spaghetti pasta, preferably made from durum wheat
*1 cup Parmesan cheese for garnish, preferably freshly grated Reggiano Parmesan 
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*Fresh ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste

==Procedure==
#Mix the coarsely chopped onion, carrot, celery and fennel (optional) together and finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] them (this is called a battuto in Italian, or a finely chopped mixture of vegetables and herbs to flavour a dish).
#Cut the ham or bacon into little cubes and sauté in a heavy [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
#Add the butter and allow it to melt. Then, add the battuto.
#Cook, stirring occasionally until very lightly browned. Add this mixture to a heavy pot.
#Heat the olive oil in the [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] the battuto was browned in and when the oil is hot, add the beef and stir to break up lumps, cooking until well browned.
#Add to the battuto in the pot.
#Add the wine to the skillet the beef was in and stir on high heat, scraping any brown bits stuck to the pan.
#Add the tomato paste and stock and stir until well mixed and add this mixture to the pot.
#Drain and coarsely chop the plum tomatoes and add them to the pot.
#Add the bay leaf and lemon rind. Bring the pot to a boil, then reduce to a gentle [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], with bubbles barely breaking the surface.
#Simmer, stirring occasionally for an hour (or more), until thick.
#Add pepper and salt to taste.
#When the sauce is ready, bring a gallon (4 litres) of water to a full boil over high heat in a large pot
#Add the pasta, give it a brisk stir to ensure it is all covered by water and not clumped together. Cook for about 10–12 minutes, or until [[Cookbook:al dente|al dente]] (firm but not hard, there should still be a bit of 'bite' when chewing pasta, rather than soggy and mushy).
#Drain the pasta well and serve immediately.
#Remove the bay leaf and lemon rind, then spoon the Bolognese sauce over the pasta and have guests garnish with the grated Parmesan cheese.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* This is a great recipe for making in large quantities and freezing. If making bulk recipes, be sure to simmer for hours, or even a full day, occasionally stirring up from the bottom of the large pot to ensure the contents at the bottom does not burn, adding stock as needed to keep the right consistency. The goal is to have the flavours mix and make the home smell delicious!
*Never rinse pasta with water. To ensure there is no excess starch from the pasta, choose a high quality durum wheat pasta and boil it in lots of water.

Cook, stirring occasionally until very lightly browned. Add this mixture to a heavy pot.
Heat the olive oil in the skillet the battuto was browned in and when the oil is hot, add the beef and stir to break up lumps, cooking until well browned.
Add to the battuto in the pot.
Add the wine to the skillet the beef was in and stir on high heat, scraping any brown bits stuck to the pan.
Add the tomato paste and stock and stir until well mixed and add this mixture to the pot.
Drain and coarsely chop the plum tomatoes and add them to the pot.
Add the bay leaf and lemon rind. Bring the pot to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, with bubbles barely breaking the surface.
Simmer, stirring occasionally for an hour (or more), until thick.
Add pepper and salt to taste.
When the sauce is ready, bring a gallon (4 litres) of water to a full boil over high heat in a large pot

Add the pasta, give it a brisk stir to ensure it is all covered by water and not clumped together. Cook for about 10–12 minutes, or until al dente (firm but not hard, there should still be a bit of 'bite' when chewing pasta, rather than soggy and mushy).
Drain the pasta well and serve immediately.
Remove the bay leaf and lemon rind, then spoon the Bolognese sauce over the pasta and have guests garnish with the grated Parmesan cheese.
recipes.notes_source_wikitext:
* This is a great recipe for making in large quantities and freezing. If making bulk recipes, be sure to simmer for hours, or even a full day, occasionally stirring up from the bottom of the large pot to ensure the contents at the bottom does not burn, adding stock as needed to keep the right consistency. The goal is to have the flavours mix and make the home smell delicious!
*Never rinse pasta with water. To ensure there is no excess starch from the pasta, choose a high quality durum wheat pasta and boil it in lots of water.

recipes.title: Basic Indian Tomato Gravy
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Sauce recipes|servings=4|time=20 minutes|difficulty=2| Image = [[File:Tomato Chutney.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

This traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] '''tomato gravy''' can be used as a base for all sorts of vegetables, boiled [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], cubed [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]] or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]. This is often referred to as a "[[Cookbook:Curry|curry]]". It is usually eaten with plain white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:Rice Recipes|rice mixtures]].

==Ingredients==
* 5 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] large
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], diced small
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Ghee|ghee]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] paste
* 5 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], pounded
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Chile|chile]] powder
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]] powder
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] powder
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

==Procedure==
# Fry the onions in hot ghee until they start to brown.
# Add the ginger and garlic and stir, then add the powdered spices. Blend well.
# Throw in the tomatoes and salt to taste.
# Turn the flame down to medium and cover for ten minutes. This will form a spicy gravy to which you can add any mixture of vegetables or boiled eggs or fried fish or chicken or lamb/goat.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* If adding cooked vegetables, keep the pot on the flame until they are uniformly heated; for uncooked vegetables, cook as long as necessary.
*With chicken/lamb/goat, add the marinated poultry/meat after frying the ginger garlic paste and adding the dry spice powders. Sear the poultry/meat on high heat, turning the pieces continuously for about 10–15 minutes until the juices get sealed inside. Add the tomatoes after this step. Continue cooking as per above recipe. Alternatively, you have the option of frying /roasting/grilling the marinated poultry/meat separately, before adding to the curry, then letting it simmer for at least 20 minutes.
* You can add a little cayenne and cumin and leave out the chili powder (though "chili powder" in Indian recipes ''is'' cayenne/powdered chilis)
* Depending on the freshness of your spices, you may want to add extra spices in the same ratio to achieve a stronger flavour.
* Generally, in Indian cuisine, for lamb or goat (known locally as 'mutton'), you can use all the above ingredients to make the gravy (curry). Some recipes use curd/yogurt, while some use tomatoes for the balancing tart flavour. With chicken, lamb and goat, marination is preferred. Also, various spice powders and spices (sabut garam masala) are added depending on the recipe. For example, cloves and cinnamon can be added to the hot oil, to give an excellent flavour.
* For a vegan version of this recipe, substitute the ghee with coconut oil or other vegetable oil.
* You can also use a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooker|pressure cooker]] instead of the stovetop; in this case, cook it for 6−7 whistles on a medium flame. This is especially useful when cooking lamb or goat as the meat is tougher than chicken. 
* You can also use fried onions as garnish to get a gravy with a different flavor. This is used frequently in chicken recipes.

recipes.title: Hermits
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Cookie recipes|servings=8|time=30 minutes|difficulty=3}}
{{nutritionsummary|1 strip (105 g)|8|364|100|11.1 g|6.4 g|19 mg|215 mg|62.4 g|0.9 g|36.1 g|4.7 g|2%|3%|2%|6%}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]]

'''Hermits''' are chewy [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]] [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spice]] [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookies]]. This version is on the strong side of the spectrum so those who prefer less hot-tasting food should hold back on the cloves and ginger.

==Ingredients==

*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (275 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/9.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*⅔ cup ({{convert|65|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) seedless [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (a handful more if you like them)
*⅔ cup ({{convert|120|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) packed dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*2½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*2 teaspoons ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ cup ({{convert|175|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) molasses 
*6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
*2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

==Procedure==

#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|375°F/190°C]].
#Line a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]] with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]].
#In a large bowl, stir together flour, raisins, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder, and salt until well combined; watch the brown sugar to ensure that it doesn't clump—it will want to do so and brown sugar clumps coated in flour look a lot like raisins coated in flour.
#Stir in molasses, butter, vanilla, and egg until fully integrated. Shape the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] in two strips (approximately {{convert|6|x|3|in|cm|abbr=on|disp=s}}) separated by at least {{convert|1.5|in|cm|abbr=on}} on the sheet pan.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 12–15 minutes, or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted into the center of the strips comes out dry.
#Allow to cool slightly then remove the hermits (on their parchment) to cooling racks to cool completely; be sure the bottoms have cooled (just reach under and feel—if its more than a little warmer than room temperature its not there yet). 
#Move the hermits (still on their parchment) to a counter for portioning and removal from parchment. Cut hermits into {{convert|1.5|in|cm|abbr=on}} wide strips (a [[Cookbook:Pizza Cutter|pizza cutter]] should work well) then carefully scrape them away from the parchment with a good thin [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]].
#Enjoy with a glass of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] or [[Cookbook:A Nice Cup of Tea|a nice cup of tea]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Although nice when warm these hermits will be even better after a night in an air-tight tin. They should last about a week.
* A buttered sheet pan works if you have no parchment, but it makes cooling and cutting more difficult and damaging to the sheet pan.

[[Category:Recipes for cookies|Hermits]]

ingredients_original: ⅔ cup (65 g) seedless raisins (a handful more if you like them)
⅔ cup (120 g) packed dark brown sugar
steps_original: Preheat oven to 375°F/190°C.
Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, raisins, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder, and salt until well combined; watch the brown sugar to ensure that it doesn't clump—it will want to do so and brown sugar clumps coated in flour look a lot like raisins coated in flour.
Stir in molasses, butter, vanilla, and egg until fully integrated. Shape the dough in two strips (approximately 6 x) separated by at least 1.5 in on the sheet pan.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the strips comes out dry.

Allow to cool slightly then remove the hermits (on their parchment) to cooling racks to cool completely; be sure the bottoms have cooled (just reach under and feel—if its more than a little warmer than room temperature its not there yet).

Move the hermits (still on their parchment) to a counter for portioning and removal from parchment. Cut hermits into 1.5 in wide strips (a pizza cutter should work well) then carefully scrape them away from the parchment with a good thin spatula.
Enjoy with a glass of milk or a nice cup of tea.

* Although nice when warm these hermits will be even better after a night in an air-tight tin. They should last about a week.
* A buttered sheet pan works if you have no parchment, but it makes cooling and cutting more difficult and damaging to the sheet pan.

recipes.title: Banana Chocolate Bread Pudding
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=6 servings|time=1 ½ hours|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Desserts|Desserts]]

Bread pudding is a British Dessert. This version has banana and chocolate. 

==Ingredients==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (20 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 0.71 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) semisweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] chips
* ⅓ cup (80 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 2.7 oz) spiced [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]]  
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] 
* 2 cups (450 ml / 15 oz) [[cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]]
* ⅓ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 1 loaf (16 oz / 450 g) [[cookbook:Baguette|French bread]] or other non-sour white [[cookbook:bread|bread]] (stale bread is traditionally used)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]  
* 3 [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]]

==Procedure==
# In a cup or other small container, add 2 tablespoons of rum to the chocolate chips and soak them until they are needed later.
# In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, whipping cream, vanilla extract, rest of rum, and 3 tablespoons sugar.
# Slice the bread, trim off the crusts and cut it into strips. Divide the bread strips into three parts.
# Butter a [[Cookbook:Loaf Pan|loaf pan]].
# Peel the bananas, cut them in half crosswise and then lengthwise.
# In a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat, melt the butter and add the banana pieces with rest of sugar. cook 2 minutes, then flip the bananas over and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
# Cover the bottom of the loaf pan with bread strips (use ⅓ of the bread strips for this).
# Spread half of the banana pieces on top of the layer of bread strips.
# Spread half of the chocolate chips on top of the bananas.
# Add another layer of bread strips.
# Pour half of the egg mix into the loaf pan and let it soak in for a minute.
# Add the rest of the bananas, then the rest of the chocolate chips, then the rest of the bread strips. pour the rest of the egg mixture on top.
# Let the loaf pan sit for about 15 minutes while preheating the oven to {{Convert|350|F|C}}.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 50 minutes. let cool for 10–15 minutes.
# Serve with rum sauce, whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

ingredients_original: ¼ cup (20 g / 0.71 oz) semisweet chocolate chips
⅓ cup (80 ml / 2.7 oz) spiced rum
⅓ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) white granulated sugar
1 loaf (16 oz / 450 g) French bread or other non-sour white bread (stale bread is traditionally used)
steps_original: In a cup or other small container, add 2 tablespoons of rum to the chocolate chips and soak them until they are needed later.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, whipping cream, vanilla extract, rest of rum, and 3 tablespoons sugar.
Slice the bread, trim off the crusts and cut it into strips. Divide the bread strips into three parts.
Butter a loaf pan.
Peel the bananas, cut them in half crosswise and then lengthwise.
In a skillet over medium heat, melt the butter and add the banana pieces with rest of sugar. cook 2 minutes, then flip the bananas over and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Cover the bottom of the loaf pan with bread strips (use ⅓ of the bread strips for this).
Spread half of the banana pieces on top of the layer of bread strips.
Spread half of the chocolate chips on top of the bananas.
Add another layer of bread strips.
Pour half of the egg mix into the loaf pan and let it soak in for a minute.
Add the rest of the bananas, then the rest of the chocolate chips, then the rest of the bread strips. pour the rest of the egg mixture on top.
Let the loaf pan sit for about 15 minutes while preheating the oven to 350 F.
Bake for 50 minutes. let cool for 10–15 minutes.
Serve with rum sauce, whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Chicken recipes
| servings = 4
| time = 1 hour
| difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:Chicken Tikka Masala Curry.png|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

'''Chicken tikka masala''' is a dish based on chunks of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]]-style roasted chicken ([[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka|Chicken Tikka]]) cooked in a [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]] [[Cookbook:Curry|curry]] sauce, originating in India. There is no standard recipe for chicken tikka masala; a survey found that, of 48 different recipes, the only common ingredient was chicken.<ref>{{cite web |author= BBC E-Cyclopedia | url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/02/99/e-cyclopedia/1285804.stm | title=Chicken tikka masala: Spice and easy does it |accessdate=28 September 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070716024029/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/02/99/e-cyclopedia/1285804.stm |archive-date=16 July 2007}}</ref> The sauce usually includes tomato and either [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut cream]] and various spices.

==Ingredients==
*675 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) cooked [[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka|Chicken Tikka]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seed oil (see notes)
*4 large cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*200 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely chopped (optional)
*1 tin (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) plum [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], chopped
*1–4 chopped fresh green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] (depending on strength of the chiles and the desired strength of the sauce)
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] chopped fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] (coriander leaves)
*50 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (4 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) single [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] malt [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or tamarind extract
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] curry paste
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Tandoori masala|tandoori masala paste]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]]

==Procedure==
#Heat the oil in a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].
#Add the garlic and onions and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] until browned.
#Add the curry pastes and mix well, adding a little water or yogurt.
#Add the cooked chicken tikka, and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] for two minutes to heat through.
#Add the tomatoes, vinegar, tomato paste, and chilies and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for five minutes. Add more extra water if needed.
#Add the cream, garam masala, and chopped cilantro and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for a few times.
#Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with [[Cookbook:Naan|Naan]], [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] coloured yellow with [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]], [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] [[Cookbook:Bahjis|bahjis]] and/or a glass of white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*[[w:Mustard oil|Mustard seed oil]] is considered inappropriate for human consumption in many parts of the world and is therefore not always available. A poor alternative can be made by crackling ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] of [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seeds in approximately 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] of very hot [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. Allow to cool, then use in place of mustard seed oil.
*Powdered or concentrated ingredients can be substituted for fresh ones but at the amount of taste.

1–4 chopped fresh green chiles (depending on strength of the chiles and the desired strength of the sauce)
1 tbsp malt vinegar or tamarind extract

Add the garlic and onions and stir-fry until browned.
Add the curry pastes and mix well, adding a little water or yogurt.
Add the cooked chicken tikka, and stir-fry for two minutes to heat through.
Add the tomatoes, vinegar, tomato paste, and chilies and simmer for five minutes. Add more extra water if needed.
Add the cream, garam masala, and chopped cilantro and simmer for a few times.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with Naan, rice coloured yellow with turmeric, onion bahjis and/or a glass of white wine.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Meat recipes|servings=6|time=1 hour|difficulty=3
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]
==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] low-fat plain [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] finely-[[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 teaspoon crushed dried [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] 93% lean [[Cookbook:Ground Beef|ground beef]]
* ½ cup cooked [[Cookbook:Rice|brown rice]]
* ⅓ cup finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* ¼ cup packed [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], chopped coriander
* ¼ cup packed flat-leaf [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], chopped

recipes.title: Gluten Veggie Meat
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Wheat recipes|servings=14–16|time=75 minutes|difficulty=3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]]

'''Gluten veggie meat''' is an excellent supplement to meatless dishes. Many store-bought vegan protein meats are made from gluten. This particular recipe is very inexpensive and can provide a family with several weeks of meat substitute that is delicious and a fraction of the cost of sustaining a diet that is exclusively animal meat.

==Ingredients==
* 1 bag (22 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]/623 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) Vital [[Cookbook:Gluten|wheat gluten]] flour
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley flakes]]
* ¾ teaspoons [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|bouillon cubes]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* ¾ teaspoons [[Cookbook:Onion Powder|onion powder]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]

==Procedure==
# In a large bowl, combine the gluten flour, garlic powder, parsley flakes, and cup of water.
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] for about 2 minutes, cover, and set aside for 10 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] gluten into pieces. The smaller the pieces, then firmer the final texture.
# Bring a large pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add bouillon cubes.
# Add sliced pieces of gluten to the seasoned, boiling water.
# Reduce heat to subtle [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover with lid and simmer for 55 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Drain substantially larger gluten pieces, and place in another bowl to cool.
# In another bowl with a lid, combine all-purpose flour, onion powder, and salt; cover and shake.
# In another bowl, pour in soy sauce for dipping.
# Dip several pieces of cooled gluten into bowl with soy sauce.
# Place gluten pieces in bowl with seasoned flour, cover, and shake.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] pieces in [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] with [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]] until browned.

recipes.title: Garlic Pork Chops with Black Mushrooms
recipes.source_title: Cookbook:Garlic Pork Chops with Black Mushrooms
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Pork recipes|servings=4|time=45 minutes|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:California cuisine|California cuisine]]

Pan fried pork chops are topped with a spicy, mushroom, and garlic sauce to make an elegant Asian-inspired dish.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Stock|pork broth]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounce]] dried black chanterelle [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Rice vinegar|rice wine vinegar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:honey|honey]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|hot-pepper flakes]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
* 1 tablespoon minced fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 4 boneless [[Cookbook:Pork|pork chops]], ½-inch thick

== Procedure ==

# Bring the chicken broth to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Add the dried mushrooms, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] over low heat for about 10 minutes. 
# In a small bowl, stir together the vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and red pepper flakes. Set aside.
# Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat. Add the pork chops, and [[Cookbook:Browning|brown]] for about 2 minutes on each side. Add the garlic and ginger; cook and stir until fragrant.
# Stir in the soy sauce mixture, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 5 minutes, uncovered.
# Remove the mushrooms from the pan using a slotted spoon, and [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]] into thin strips. Stir the mushrooms and chicken broth into the pan with the pork chops, and simmer uncovered over low heat until the sauce has reduced by about ⅓, and the pork chops are cooked through.
# To serve, place pork chops onto serving plates, and spoon mushroom sauce over them.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When doubling recipe, don't double vinegar or red pepper flakes—use ⅛ more of each.
* When combining vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and red pepper flakes, let it [[Cookbook:Macerating|macerate]] for 5 minutes, then check for balance/taste.
* Try pre-[[Cookbook:Brining|brining]] pork.
* Add baby [[Cookbook:Bok Choy|bok choy]] or replace the mushrooms with the baby bok choy.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary

| difficulty = 2
| Image = [[File:Dinuguan and Puto.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Philippines|Cuisine of the Philippines]]

'''Dinuguan''' (pork blood stew) or '''dinardaraan''' in Ilocano is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Philippines|Filipino]] dish usually made from the blood, entrails and meat of a pig. It is sometimes known as "[[Cookbook:chocolate|chocolate]] meat" as the stew has a thick chocolate-like color and consistency. The name "dinuguan" is derived from the Filipino word "dugo", meaning blood. Likewise, in Ilocano, "dinardaraan" is derived from "dara", meaning blood. Dinuguan has more liquid, while dinardaraan is drier. It is most often served over [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] or puto (sweet steamed rice [[Cookbook:muffin|muffins]]).

==Ingredients==
*3 [[cookbook:cup|cup]]s (700 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Cubing|cubed]] boneless [[cookbook:pork|pork]] butt with fat 
*3 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoon]]s [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]] or [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]] 
*½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] mixed with 1 cup (240 ml) [[Cookbook:Water|water]] and 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] 
*1 medium-sized yellow [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*1½ cups (360 ml) [[cookbook:pork|pork blood]] (Ideally from [[cookbook:cuisine of Vietnam|Vietnamese]], Filipino or Western European markets) 
*3 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], peeled and crushed 
*2 hot [[cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño peppers]], seeded and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]

== Preparation ==
#Place the pork in a 4-quart (560 ml) covered stove-top [[Cookbook:Casserole|casserole dish]] and add the vinegar mixture. Bring to a [[cookbook:Boil|boil]] and reduce the heat. 
#Cook, covered, for about an hour, until the pork is tender. Make sure that the liquid doesn't dry out. Add more water if necessary. 
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] and add the lard or oil. 
# When the oil is hot enough, [[cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the onion and garlic until the onion appears translucent. Remove from heat. 
#Add the oil, garlic, and onion to the pork and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
#[[cookbook:Purée|Purée]] the pork blood in a [[cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]]. 
#Add the blood to the pork gradually while stirring the mixture. Bring to a boil. 
#Add the chopped pepper and [[cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] uncovered to reduce the sauce until desired thickness is achieved. Keep covered and serve hot.

When the oil is hot enough, sauté the onion and garlic until the onion appears translucent. Remove from heat.
Add the oil, garlic, and onion to the pork and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Purée the pork blood in a food processor.
Add the blood to the pork gradually while stirring the mixture. Bring to a boil.
Add the chopped pepper and simmer uncovered to reduce the sauce until desired thickness is achieved. Keep covered and serve hot.

recipes.title: Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Chili Chicken)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| Cuisine = Peruvian
| servings = 8
| time = About 45 minutes
| difficulty = 2
| Image = [[Image:Ají de gallina (gourmet)-b.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Peru|Cuisine of Peru]]

'''''{{lang|es|Ají de Gallina}}''''' (Spanish for chili pepper chicken) is a traditional Peruvian dish which has its roots in the social upheaval of the French Revolution in 1789.<ref>[http://friendseat.com/Aji-de-Gallina-Recipe Info on ''ají de gallina'' recipe on the Friends Eat website]</ref> 

Chefs working for wealthy families lost their jobs after French aristocrats were imprisoned and executed. Some of these chefs travelled to the New World, including Peru, bringing with them French culinary expertise. Wealthy Peruvian creole families hired them to demonstrate their wealth to the ruling Spaniards.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gill |first1=Nicholas |title=Aji de gallina |url=http://newworldreview.com/tag/aji-de-gallina/ |website= newworldreview.com |access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> The fusion of local cuisines with French cooking traditions led to many new recipes, including ''ají de gallina''. 

This is a shredded chicken dish in a spicy sauce flavored with cheese, garlic, nuts and Peruvian chili peppers.<ref>[http://www.grouprecipes.com/29399/aji-de-gallina.html Info on ''ají de gallina'' recipe on the Group Recipes website]</ref> Peruvians love eating this dish on cold days.

The dish is often referred to as ''ají de pollo'' when it is prepared with frayed chicken breasts — especially nowadays in which, unlike egg hens raised traditionally on farm lots, the poultry industry breeds caged birds for meat within three months.<ref>[http://recetasdecomidaperuana.org/aji-de-gallina-para-10-porciones.html Info on ''ají de gallina'' recipe on Peruvian recipes website]</ref>

==Ingredients==
* 1300 g (4 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]]
* 120 ml (½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) of [[cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]]
* 1 large finely chopped [[cookbook:onion|onion]] 
* 8 cloves of minced [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* 3 hot [[cookbook: Aji amarillo|yellow South American chilis]] (seeds and filaments removed): Adjust quantity for individual taste.
* [[cookbook:Salt|Salt]] and [[cookbook:pepper|pepper]] to taste 
* 1 [[cookbook:Stock|chicken stock]] cube
* ¼ loaf of [[cookbook:bread|bread]]
* 110 g (¼ lb) of chopped [[cookbook:pecan|pecans]]
* 110 g (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]])  grated [[cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
* 1 can of [[cookbook:evaporated milk|evaporated milk]] 
* 1.6 kg (3.5 lbs) boiled [[cookbook:rice|rice]] (flavored with chopped garlic and salt)
* 4 hard boiled [[cookbook:egg|eggs]]
* 6 [[cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] 
* 120 g (½ cup) [[cookbook:Olive|black olives]]

==Preparation==
#[[cookbook:Boil|Boil]] chicken in salted water together with the stock cube. Remove bones and break into bite size pieces, keeping the resulting chicken stock. 
#In a [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]], heat oil and [[cookbook:sauté|sauté]] the onion, garlic, and finely chopped chili peppers and add salt and pepper. Fry this until the onions are cooked and golden.
#Soak the bread in two cups of the stock from the boiled chicken and place in a [[cookbook:blender|blender]] for a couple of minutes and then add the resulting liquid to the saucepan. 
#Cook slowly for ten minutes. Cook slowly, stirring to thicken.
#While the Ají de Gallina is cooking slowly, boil the rice: first fry the garlic for a couple of seconds, then add the rice and the salt, then add the water. When the water starts to boil, let the rice cook in a closed pot very slowly for about 20 minutes or until the water has completely evaporated (hint: to cook "peruvian" rice: cook a cup of rice in two cups of water).
#Back to the Ají de Gallina: add the chopped pecans, grated cheese, and chicken pieces. Cook until it has a thick creamy texture. About five minutes before serving, add the evaporated milk and continue cooking on low heat.
#Serve over the boiled rice and garnish with halved potatoes, eggs quartered lengthwise, and olives.

==References==

ingredients_original: 3 hot yellow South American chilis (seeds and filaments removed): Adjust quantity for individual taste.
1.6 kg (3.5 lbs) boiled rice (flavored with chopped garlic and salt)
steps_original: Boil chicken in salted water together with the stock cube. Remove bones and break into bite size pieces, keeping the resulting chicken stock.
In a saucepan, heat oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and finely chopped chili peppers and add salt and pepper. Fry this until the onions are cooked and golden.
Soak the bread in two cups of the stock from the boiled chicken and place in a blender for a couple of minutes and then add the resulting liquid to the saucepan.
Cook slowly for ten minutes. Cook slowly, stirring to thicken.

While the Ají de Gallina is cooking slowly, boil the rice: first fry the garlic for a couple of seconds, then add the rice and the salt, then add the water. When the water starts to boil, let the rice cook in a closed pot very slowly for about 20 minutes or until the water has completely evaporated (hint: to cook "peruvian" rice: cook a cup of rice in two cups of water).

Back to the Ají de Gallina: add the chopped pecans, grated cheese, and chicken pieces. Cook until it has a thick creamy texture. About five minutes before serving, add the evaporated milk and continue cooking on low heat.
Serve over the boiled rice and garnish with halved potatoes, eggs quartered lengthwise, and olives.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Squash recipes|servings=2|time=45 minutes|difficulty=2}}{{recipe}}

'''Acorn squash with orange marmalade''' is a quick, easy vegetable side dish that has great appeal due to its slight sweetness.

==Ingredients==
*1 medium [[Cookbook:Acorn Squash|acorn squash]], halved lengthwise
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Marmalade|orange marmalade]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*⅛ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C). 
#Remove seeds and strings from squash halves. 
#Cut a small piece off outside of each half to make a flat space on which the half can stand level. 
#Place halves in a shallow pan or casserole in ¼ inch (6 mm) water with insides facing down. Bake for 35 minutes.
#Combine marmalade and butter in a small bowl. 
#Remove squash from oven, and invert in pan or dish. Salt lightly.
#Spread marmalade and butter mixture on edges of squash, allowing excess to run into center. 
#Place under broiler for 5 minutes or until lightly browned.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Substitute [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]] for the orange marmalade.

recipes.title: Rosemary and Citrus Cordial
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Beverage recipes|servings=20|yield=2 cups ({{convert|500|ml|USpt|abbr=on|disp=s}})|time=30 minutes|difficulty=2}}{{Recipe}}

This recipe for '''rosemary and citrus cordial''' is adapted from page 26 of the April 2023 edition of Tesco's magazine.

== Ingredients ==
*1 red [[Cookbook:Grapefruit|grapefruit]], scrubbed
*3 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], scrubbed
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (20 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/0.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Rosemary|rosemary]]
*{{convert|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} piece [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] thinly
*⅔ cup ({{convert|150|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|superfine sugar]]
*1 cup (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]/8.5 fl oz) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*[[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Fizzy water]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Whiskey|Whiskey]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Using a peeler, remove long strips of peel from grapefruit and 2 of lemons. Be careful not to remove any of white pith.
#Put the peels into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Juice the lemons and grapefruit, and add the juice to the pan.
#Using a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]], roll over the rosemary sprigs a few times on a [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|chopping board]] to release the oils.
#Add the rosemary to the pan with ginger, sugar, and water.
#Heat for 5 minutes over a low-medium heat, stirring occasionally, to dissolve the sugar.
#Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes until you get a slightly thick [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]. Leave it to cool, then use immediately or chill overnight to develop the flavors.
#[[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the cordial syrup through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] into a bowl or jug. Transfer to a bottle.
#To use, mix 1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of cordial into ⅔ cup ({{convert|160|ml|USoz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) of fizzy water to make a soda, or add to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] water with 2 tablespoons of whiskey to make a hot toddy.

[[Category:Recipes for beverages]]
[[Category:Recipes using lemon]]
[[Category:Recipes using grapefruit]]
[[Category:Recipes using superfine sugar]]
[[Category:Recipes using carbonated water]]
[[Category:Recipes using fresh ginger]]
steps_original: Using a peeler, remove long strips of peel from grapefruit and 2 of lemons. Be careful not to remove any of white pith.
Put the peels into a saucepan. Juice the lemons and grapefruit, and add the juice to the pan.
Using a rolling pin, roll over the rosemary sprigs a few times on a chopping board to release the oils.
Add the rosemary to the pan with ginger, sugar, and water.
Heat for 5 minutes over a low-medium heat, stirring occasionally, to dissolve the sugar.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes until you get a slightly thick syrup. Leave it to cool, then use immediately or chill overnight to develop the flavors.
Strain the cordial syrup through a sieve into a bowl or jug. Transfer to a bottle.
To use, mix 1–2 tablespoons of cordial into ⅔ cup (160 ml) of fizzy water to make a soda, or add to boiling water with 2 tablespoons of whiskey to make a hot toddy.

recipes.title: Pan-fried Ravioli
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Pasta recipes|servings=12|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Pasta|Pasta]]

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] Italian seasoned [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)
* ½ package (25 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) frozen [[Cookbook:Ravioli|ravioli]], thawed
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] for [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
* 1 jar (16 ounces) [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]]

==Procedure==
# Combine milk and egg in a small bowl. 
# Place breadcrumbs and salt in a shallow bowl.
# Dip ravioli in milk mixture, and coat with breadcrumbs.
# In a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat marinara sauce over medium heat until bubbling, about 5–10 minutes. Reduce the heat to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# In a large heavy pan, pour oil to depth of 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]]. Heat oil over medium heat to 375°F. 
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] ravioli in hot oil, a few at a time, for about 1 minute on each side or until golden.
# Drain on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]]. 
# Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and serve immediately with hot marinara sauce.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* You can use cheese or meat raviolis, but the traditional version is made out of a square meat ravioli.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast Recipes|Breakfast Recipes]]

A delicious '''bran muffin''' recipe that makes an excellent [[Cookbook:Breakfast Recipes|breakfast]].

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) natural [[Cookbook:Wheat Bran|wheat bran]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 ml) cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 ml) [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Muffin Pan|Muffin cups]], greased or lined
* [[Cookbook:Measuring Cup|Measuring cup]]
* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]

==Procedure==
#Stir wheat bran and buttermilk together in a [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]].
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together egg, brown sugar and margarine in another mixing bowl. 
#Combine remaining ingredients in a third bowl. Add to [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]], and stir just to moisten.
#Fill muffin cups ¾ full.
#Bake at [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]] (200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*For bran raisin muffins, add 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]].
*If you do not want to buy store-bought cultured buttermilk, you can make your own by adding 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] or [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] to 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]. Let it sit for five minutes before using.
*Tastes best when still warm.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

==Ingredients==

* 2 cans (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) fat-free vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1 bag (1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]]) frozen [[Cookbook:Mixed vegetables|mixed vegetables]]
* 1 can (14½ ounces) no-salt-added [[Cookbook:Stew|stewed]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* ⅓ cup broken [[cookbook:Pasta|angel-hair pasta]], in 1- to 2-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] lengths

* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic powder]]

==Procedure==

# Pour broth and water into a 4½-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]] or soup pot.
# Place pot over high heat.
# While liquid is heating, add frozen vegetables, stewed tomatoes with their juices and uncooked pasta.
# Cover pot and bring to [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]].
# Meanwhile, rinse and drain beans.
# When soup comes to a boil, uncover it and stir well. Scrape the pot with a [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|wooden spoon]] to loosen any pasta.
# Add beans, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder.
# Reduce heat to medium-high or medium, maintaining a moderate boil.
# Stir frequently and cook until pasta is tender, about 5 minutes.
# Reduce heat to low and add Parmesan.
# Stir occasionally and simmer for 5 minutes to develop the flavor.
# Serve at once or simmer on low until ready to serve.

recipes.title: Ertesuppe (Pea Soup)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Soup recipes|servings=12|time=Overnight plus 2 hours|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Norway|Cuisine of Norway]]

'''Ertesuppe''' ('''pea soup''') is a [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] using dry yellow Swedish split peas and the butt portion of ham.

==Ingredients==
*16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] [[Cookbook:Pea|split yellow Swedish peas]]
*12 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*2–3 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] s[[Cookbook:Ham|moked pork butt]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|yellow onion]], peeled and chopped
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]

==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|Soak]] the dry peas overnight in about 4 cups of cold water.
# Add 8 cups of water to the peas and soaking water. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the peas in a pot until soft.
# In a separate pot, [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the smoked butt for 40 minutes per pound.
# Cut the smoked butt into small cubes, and add to the softened pea stock.
# Add the onion and half the salt and pepper. Adjust to taste, and mix in the thyme. 
# Cook for at least 5 minutes together, adding water from the meat if the stock is too thick. Cook longer if it is too thin. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Serve immediately, or chill and reheat for the next day. Serve as dinner course, or with bread for a simple meal.

recipes.title: Scheiterhaufen (Austrian Bread Pudding)
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Austrian recipes
| servings = 6
| time = 60 minutes
| difficulty = 2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]]

'''Scheiterhaufen''' (literally "funeral pyre" or "stake") is a type of traditional sweet dish in Austria and Southern Germany. It was mentioned for the first time in a Roman cookbook in the 1st century AD by Marcus Gravius Apicius. In 1691 it first appeared in a German cookbook under the name ''Güldene Schnitten'' (golden slices). The term ''Armer Ritter'' (poor knight) was first used in 1787 and had its breakthrough in the 19th century.

The name possibly refers to the way the slices of bread and fruit are layered to make this dish, which seems representative of the way in which ancient cultures used to pile up chunks of wood to make a funeral pyre. The name could also refer to the way the dish looks when served, since it tends to fall apart when put on a plate. Other names for Austrian and German variations are ''Rostiger Ritter'', ''Fotzelschnitten'', ''Semmelschnitten'', ''Kartäuserklöße'', ''Weckschnitten'', ''Gebackener Weck'', ''Pofesen'', or ''Blinder Fisch''. 

The dish is similar to the English ''poor knights of Windsor'' in England, Russian ''grenki'', Dutch ''wentelteefje'', American ''French toast'', French ''pain perdu'', Portuguese ''rabanadas'', and Spanish ''torrijas''.

==Ingredients==
* 17.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) stale white [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Peach|peaches]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] (60 g) refined [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* 2 cups (½ [[Cookbook:Liter|L]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (20 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]] or a few drops of rum aroma
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

==Procedure==
# Wash the apples and peaches, and peel them if desired. Cut them into [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]] approximately ¼ inch (1 cm) thick.
# Cut the bread into slices about the same size as the fruit.
# Pour the milk into a bowl and add the eggs. Mix well. Then take the slices of bread and let them soak in the mixture for a few seconds. This will take longer if you use stale rather than fresh bread.
# Mix the refined sugar and the cinnamon in a cup or a small bowl.
# Grease an [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|ovenproof dish]], then layer the slices, bread, and fruit alternately in the dish. Sprinkle a bit of the sugar-cinnamon mixture on top of every layer. For the best result, start and end with a layer of bread. You can decide whether you want an apple and a peach layer or whether you would like to mix the different kinds of fruit. 
# Scatter a few flakes of butter on top, and put the dish into the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 45 minutes at 180°C/350°F.
# Enjoy!

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*This recipe is rather a guideline; you can alter it according to your taste and wishes. Generally, there is not only one recipe for Scheiterhaufen, as people in former times were forced to use what they had available.
*You can take any kind of white bread you like, stale or fresh. You can use any kind of white bread that you have on-hand, but for an extra soft Scheiterhaufen, something like the white bread used for toast yields the best result. One variation is to roast the bread in a pan with a bit of butter before layering it (in this case you would have to pour the milk-egg-rum mixture on top of your layers).
*You can use other kinds of fruit to suit your taste, but the traditional Austrian Scheiterhaufen recipe uses only apples. [[Cookbook:Plum|Plums]] are also a good choice, but frankly, you can use any fruit of the season. The selection above is a summer variation.
*Some cooks like to add nuts like [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]] or [[Cookbook:Hazelnut|hazelnuts]] to create a distinctive taste. You can also add [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]; they are often used together with apples in Austrian cuisine.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{Recipe}}{{recipesummary
| Category = Beverages

| Difficulty = 2
| Energy = 80 kcal/100 g
| Rating = 
}}

'''Jamaican sorrel soda''' is a traditional Jamaican carbonated drink consisting of sweetened hibiscus tea with added ginger.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 ml) water
* 3 [[Cookbook:Roselle|hibiscus]] (roselle) tea bags or 3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (15 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) dried hibiscus
* 6 [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]] ¼ in (0.67 cm) cubes of [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] (optional)
* ½ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]], as needed

== Procedure ==

# Combine the water, hibiscus, and ginger in a pot. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] for about 15 minutes.
# Remove and discard the hibiscus and ginger.
# Stir the sugar into the liquid, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until you have about 5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (150 ml) [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]].
# Remove from the heat and let cool.
# To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of sparkling water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

recipes.title: Apple Tapioca
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=6|time=1–6 hours|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]]

The combination of fruit and tapioca is popular with many people. Peaches and apples, either fresh or canned, are used most often for this purpose. For this recipe, the apples should be somewhat sour, as there will then be more character to the dessert. Canned or fresh peaches or canned pineapple may be used in exactly the same way as apples. If canned fruit is used, not so much sugar nor baking in the oven will be necessary.

==Ingredients==
*¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] pearl [[Cookbook:Tapioca|tapioca]] or ½ cup minute (instant) tapioca
*2 cups boiling water
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

==Procedure==
#If pearl tapioca is used, soak it for 4 or 5 hours and then drain off all the water. Minute tapioca will need no soaking. Add the tapioca to the boiling water and salt.
#Cook in a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]] until the tapioca is entirely transparent. 
#Peel and core the apples. Place them in a buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]], fill each cavity with sugar and cinnamon, and place a piece of butter on top of each. 
#Pour the hot tapioca over these, place in a hot oven, and bake until the apples are soft. 
#Serve either hot or cold with sugar and cream.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* This recipe was copied from "Woman's Institute Library of Cookery, Vol. 4: Volume 4: Salads and Sandwiches; Cold and Frozen Desserts; Cakes, Cookies and Puddings; Pastries and Pies" found at http://www.gutenberg.net/etext06/8loc410h.htm and wikified for this cookbook.

==Ingredients==

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta cheese]]

* 1 package store-bought pizza dough

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]] (200°C).
# Combine ricotta, mozzarella, toppings, and oregano.
# Roll the pizza dough between 2 pieces of waxed paper.
# Spoon the cheese mixture into the center of the dough.
# Moisten edges of dough slightly. Fold the dough over, and seal edges by pressing with a fork.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until golden brown, about 10 or 12 minutes.
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]].

steps_original: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Beat eggs, water, and approximately soy sauce together in a bowl and set aside.
Get a large bowl and mix the ground beef and stuffing together. Make sure to use your hands and combine the mixture well, as this is the most important step.
Slowly work the egg mixture into the meat and stuffing, once again making sure to combine all ingredients well.
Pick up the big ball of meat and pack in hands until you have formed a loaf. Place in ungreased loaf pan.
Bake, uncovered, on the center rack of the oven for 45–55 minutes until center of meatloaf is browned.

'''Maitorieska''' (''milk rieska'', pronounced "RE-ehskuh") is a [[Cookbook:Barley|barley]]-based [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] that is a local specialty and a very traditional food in the Ylivieska area of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Finland|Finland]].

==Ingredients==

* 250 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) cold [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 250–330 ml (1–1½ cups) [[Cookbook:Barley|barley]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 300°C (570°F), or as high as it will go. 
# Combine milk and salt, and add flour. Mix the ingredients well to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Knead|Knead]] into a flat, round bread (about 0.5 cm / ¼ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick). 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] on an [[Cookbook:Oven Tray|oven tray]] for about 10 minutes or until the surface gets some darker spots. Alternatively, [[Cookbook:Pan fry|fry it in a pan]] on the stove or on open fire.
# Eat fresh with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] and cold milk.

'''Saj bread''' (Arabic: خبز الصاج) is a thin, unleavened flatbread baked on a griddle known as a ''saj''.

== Ingredients ==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[cookbook:water|water]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix flour and water, adding water gradually, until left with a workable [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] thoroughly.
# Cover the dough and let rest for about 5 minutes. Add salt.
# Separate from dough smaller portions and make into balls. Using a flat surface lined with flour, begin to [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] each ball into a flat piece of dough.
# Place flattened dough on [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] and bake until tender. On a heated griddle, cooking only takes a few seconds. Flip-over and cook the other side for only a few seconds.
# Remove from griddle and allow to cool. Fold and store.

'''Cauliflower with breadcrumbs''' is a popular dish and side-dish in Poland and many parts of Central Europe. It's really simple to make.

==Ingredients==

recipes.title: Pumpkin Risotto
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Rice recipes|servings=6 persons|time=2 hours|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday]] | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]

==Ingredients==

* 1½ [[Cookbook:pound|pound]]s (650 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:pumpkin|pumpkin]] or winter [[Cookbook:squash|squash]], whole
* ½ [[Cookbook:teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 6 grinds freshly cracked [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 bunch fresh [[Cookbook:marjoram|marjoram]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] (some reserved for garnish)
* 2 [[Cookbook:clove|cloves]] [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], peeled and thickly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:olive Oil|olive oil]], divided
* 1 [[Cookbook:quart|quart]] (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]/broth
* 10 tablespoons unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] at room temperature, divided
* 1 medium red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]]s (360 g) [[Cookbook:risotto|risotto]] [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 5 tablespoons extra-dry white [[Cookbook:Vermouth|vermouth]]
* 1½ cups (360 g) [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmiggiano Reggiano]], finely grated, plus extra to sprinkle at the table

==Preparation==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (210°C).
# Remove seeds and fiber from inside the pumpkin and cut into chunks. Place skin side down on a [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] [[Cookbook:Brush|brushed]] with a little olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, scatter the marjoram and garlic over the pieces, cover with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] about 45 minutes, or until soft. 
# Remove from oven and allow to cool. Cut the flesh from skin into small cubes and reserve the baking juices.
# Heat the chicken stock and check for seasoning.
# Melt 6 tablespoons butter and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]] or pot. Add onion and gently [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until soft. Add rice and stir until completely covered in oil. Then, add vermouth and stir until it is absorbed by the rice.
# Turn heat to medium-high and begin adding stock, ½ cup (120 ml) at a time, and stir until stock is completely absorbed by the rice. Continue this process until all the stock is incorporated.
# Stir in remaining butter in small pieces, pumpkin with its juices, and cheese. Serve immediately with a sprinkle of cheese and fresh marjoram to garnish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Risotto rice refers to plump, medium grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] that contains a lot of starch. Arborio or Carnaroli rices are traditionally best. Other rices that work well include Roma, Vialone, Nano and Maratelli.

'''''Escargots à la bourguignonne''''' is a French dish of snails with garlic butter.

==Ingredients==

==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 400°F.
# Drain and rinse the snails.
# Combine the butter with the shallots, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper, and blend well.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the mushroom caps, if using, in a small amount of garlic butter until cooked but still firm. Remove from the heat.
# If using snail shells, place a snail in each shell and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter. If using a snail dish without the shells, place a snail in each indentation and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter. If using mushroom caps, place 2–3 snails in each cap and top with a generous amount of garlic butter.

recipes.title: Peach and Tomato Gazpacho
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|category=Soup recipes|servings=4|time=20 minutes|difficulty=2}}{{recipe}}

This '''peach and tomato gazpacho''' is a cold [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] that is  wonderful to taste and refreshing to serve during the warmer months. The peach flavor adds a variation on the traditional more Spanish combination of tomato, bell pepper, and cucumber. Gazpacho is popular throughout Spain, Portugal, and Latin America. This particular version is more modern and is especially easy to make as little chopping is needed if you use the blender as described.

==Ingredients==
*4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (946 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 630 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*2 cups (473 ml / 1 lb / 454 g) pitted [[Cookbook:Peach|peaches]]
*¼ cup (59 ml) crushed ice
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] (30 ml) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]]
*2 Tbsp (30 ml) [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (22 ml)  white-wine [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
*1 Tbsp (15 ml / 8 sprigs) chopped fresh [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|t]]<nowiki/>sp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:pepper|black pepper]]

==Equipment==

* Medium-sized bowl
* Small-sized bowl
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]] (strong enough to chop ice)
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]] for cutting vegetables
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Measuring cups
* Measuring spoons
* [[Cookbook:Scale|Scale]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Cut the tomato into sections, place ⅔ into the blender, and set the other ⅓ to the side in the small bowl.
#Run the blender on high speed to [[Cookbook:Puréeing|purée]] the tomatoes.
#Cut the pitted peaches into sections, place ½ into the blender, and set the other ½ to the side in the small bowl.
#Add the peaches to the tomato purée and blend on high speed to purée the peaches.
#Cut the shallot into sections, place into the mixture, and purée.
#Chop the fresh tarragon, removing and discarding any large stems, place the leaves into the blender mixture, and purée.
#Add olive oil, white wine vinegar, tarragon, salt, and pepper to blender and mix well.
#Add crushed ice into the blender and purée for 30 seconds on highest power.
#Add contents from small bowl into blender and pulse on lowest setting very briefly (this will provide some texture to gazpacho with small chunks of tomato and peach).
#Serve right away as chilled gazpacho soup.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*For [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]], sprinkle some fresh tarragon leaves on the gazpacho.
*To add some variety, add a dollop of Greek [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]] to the center.
*You can purée all the ingredients in one batch, then add the ice and blend to make a smoothie.
*You can substitute a red onion for shallot.

steps_original: Cut the tomato into sections, place ⅔ into the blender, and set the other ⅓ to the side in the small bowl.
Run the blender on high speed to purée the tomatoes.
Cut the pitted peaches into sections, place ½ into the blender, and set the other ½ to the side in the small bowl.
Add the peaches to the tomato purée and blend on high speed to purée the peaches.
Cut the shallot into sections, place into the mixture, and purée.
Chop the fresh tarragon, removing and discarding any large stems, place the leaves into the blender mixture, and purée.
Add olive oil, white wine vinegar, tarragon, salt, and pepper to blender and mix well.
Add crushed ice into the blender and purée for 30 seconds on highest power.
Add contents from small bowl into blender and pulse on lowest setting very briefly (this will provide some texture to gazpacho with small chunks of tomato and peach).
Serve right away as chilled gazpacho soup.

steps_original: Wash and dry the strawberries and lemon.
Slice strawberries into small pieces.
Combine strawberries and sugar.
Roll a lemon on a counter while applying pressure with the palm of one hand. Cut lemon in half and squeeze both halves through a strainer into the strawberry mixture.
Remove any remaining seeds from the lemon halves and add them, with the rind, to the strawberry mixture.
Allow strawberry mixture to macerate for 1–2 hours, stirring occasionally until all of the sugar crystals are dissolved.
Discard lemon halves, then orange liqueur to the strawberry mixture.
Use a blender or food processor to reduce the strawberry mixture to a purée, but don't over-blend.
Stir the Greek yogurt into to the strawberry mixture, mixing until well combined.
Refrigerate strawberry yogurt mixture for at 4 four hours.
Pour strawberry yogurt mixture into a prepared ice cream maker, and mix for approximately 20 minutes, or until the frozen yogurt has reached a firm consistency.
Eat immediately, or freeze for later.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary

| Yield = About 2 quarts (1.9 L)

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|USA]] | [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|Ice Cream]]

'''Rocky road''' is a popular [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]] flavor in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|United States]]. Though there are variations on the flavor, it is traditionally composed of chocolate ice cream, [[Cookbook:Nuts and seeds|nuts]] and marshmallows. The flavor is claimed to have been created in 1929 by William Dreyer when he cut up [[cookbook:almond|almond]] and marshmallows with his wife's sewing scissors and added them to his chocolate ice cream during the Great Depression. The company claims it was then so named "to give folks something to smile about in the midst of the Great Depression."<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.dreyersinc.com/about/WebHistory.pdf| title = Dreyer's History| accessdate = April 5|accessyear = 2006}}</ref>

Alternately, Fenton's Creamery in Oakland, California, claims that William Dreyer based his recipe on a Rocky Road ice cream invented by his friend, Fenton's George Farren, who blended his Rocky Road candy bar into ice cream; however Dreyer substituted pecans for almonds.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.fentonscreamery.com/blender.html| title = Fenton's Blender Club:Rocky Road Ice Cream| accessdate = April 5| accessyear = 2006}}</ref>
 
== Ingredients ==
*⅓ [[cookbook:cup|cup]] (50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 1.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) unsweetened [[cookbook:cocoa powder|cocoa powder]]
*1 cup (200 g / 7.1 oz) white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
*2 cups (500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 1 US [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]]) [[cookbook:milk|milk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
*2 cups (450 ml / 15 oz) [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
*1 oz (28 g) semisweet [[cookbook:chocolate|chocolate]] square
*1 cup (80 g / 2.8 oz) miniature [[cookbook:marshmallow|marshmallow]]s
*½ cup (40 g / 1.4 oz) chopped [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]] or [[Cookbook:Pecan|pecans]]

==Procedure==
#In a large [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]], mix cocoa powder and sugar.
#Gradually stir in milk. Stir over low heat until sugar and cocoa dissolve.
#Cool to room temperature.
#Stir in vanilla, salt, and whipping cream; set aside.
#Shred chocolate with coarse side of [[Cookbook:Grater|grater]].

* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] whole [[Cookbook:Milkfish|milkfish]]

recipes.title: Chicken Parmigiana
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Chicken recipes|servings=2|time=30 minutes|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|US Cuisine]]

'''Chicken parmigiana''' is a popular [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]]-[[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American]] dish served in a variety of ways. The same basic recipe works for a number of dishes. The components usually consists of a breaded, tenderized piece of [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] (or slice of [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]]), a simple [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]], and [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (usually [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]]). A thicker [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]], such as linguini, a toasted loaf of Italian [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], and a light red wine such as Chianti complement this dish well.

This recipe is typical of the parmigiana recipes from New York and New Jersey.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 teaspoon of [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ a teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* ¼ teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* ¼ teaspoon of finely-crushed [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* ½ a [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato puree]]
* ¼ cup of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]] (see below if you wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]])
* ½ a cup of shredded [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
* ¼ a cup of grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano cheese]]

==Procedure==
#In a heavy [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] (preferably cast iron), heat the oil on medium heat.
#While the oil is heating, use a tenderizing mallet (or the ball of your hand) to pound the chicken breasts to about ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick. This step is important to ensure the chicken is tender and more importantly to ensure the chicken cooks thoroughly.
# Season the chicken breasts with salt and garlic powder.
# [[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] the breasts in flour and shake off any excess.
# Place both breasts in the heated oil for 3 minutes, then flip and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for an additional 2 minutes.
# Remove the breasts and place on a rack or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]].
# Preheat a [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]].
# In a large oven-safe [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the tomato puree and chicken stock until it begins to [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmer]].
# Add the oregano, basil, and pepper to saucepan and mix
# Place cooked chicken breasts in pan and flip a number of times to coat with sauce.
# Add mozzarella and parmigiana cheese to the tops of the breasts.
# Broil for 30–60 seconds. It will burn very quickly, so check it frequently.
# Remove from oven and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Use thin-sliced chicken cutlets (available at most supermarkets) to avoid the BIG mess and time of pounding.
* If [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] is to be served with this meal, it should be timed so that the parmigiana is done right when the pasta is. The pasta should be removed directly from the pot and placed into the pan. The remaining sauce can then be used with the pasta.
* This recipe works best with breasts that come from slightly older chickens (such as broiler or fryer chickens). These chickens have a stronger taste but are generally tougher.  The tenderizing step takes care of the toughness of the older birds though.
* If you do not live in area where fresh tomatoes are grown, canned tomatoes are usually superior to the low-cost ones you will find in the supermarket.

* For [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] parmigiana, follow the same steps except do not tenderize.  Veal is already tender enough.  The veal can also be cooked for 2 minutes on each side.
* Omit the tenderizing step for [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] parmigiana.
* If you want to use fresh garlic instead of powder, add it to the sauce instead of adding it to the chicken breast.
* You can also try using other types of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheeses]] such as [[Cookbook:Provolone Cheese|provolone cheese]] or [[Cookbook:Fontina Cheese|fontina cheese]] to add more of a "tasty kick" compared to a mild cheese like mozzarella 
* You may wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. When frying with olive oil, be sure to use a cheap solvent-extracted grade! The fancy grades can not tolerate heat. They have [[Cookbook:Smoke Point|smoke points]] as low as 200°F (93°C), making for both a fire hazard and a source of smoke. Save the cold-pressed extra-virgin olive oil for a [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]].

While the oil is heating, use a tenderizing mallet (or the ball of your hand) to pound the chicken breasts to about ½ inch thick. This step is important to ensure the chicken is tender and more importantly to ensure the chicken cooks thoroughly.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and garlic powder.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried White Brined Cheese (Saganaki)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|
| Category = Greek recipes
| Servings = 1
| Time = 5 minutes
| Rating = 2
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[Image:Saganaki.jpg|300px]]
}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Greece|Cuisine of Greece]] | [[Cookbook:Appetizers|Appetizers]]

'''Saganaki''' is a Greek or Greek-American dish consisting of a [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|hard, white, brined cheese]] cooked simply with olive oil in a hot pan (traditionally a two-handed vessel whence the name of the dish), usually served with [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]. In American restaurants, it is sometimes flambeed with various liqueurs at the table. In Greece, it is a traditional dish to have both with liquor (as a [[wikipedia:meze|meze]]) or at the beginning of the meal to whet the appetite. 

==Ingredients==
*1 large slice of salty, brined white [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (e.g. [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta]], sirene)
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] (''not'' extra virgin)
*1 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] wedge
*A small amount of [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Bread|Pita or other bread]] (optional) 

==Procedure==
#Heat a small [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium-high heat.
#While the pan heats, cut the cheese into slices of the desired size and thickness. Thicker slices will take longer to melt through and may result in burning, while thinner ones will have less chance to brown. 
#Optionally, dredge the slices in flour—this will create a darker and slightly crispier crust, but is an optional step as the cheese will acquire a very slight crust on its own by virtue of the oil and high heat. It will also reduce the spitting somewhat.
#Add the oil to the hot pan and swirl it around. When the oil shimmers and seems to become more fluid, it is ready. Add the cheese and step back—it will spit due to the brine-water on the cheese.
#Flip the cheese after a minute or two. A slice of ¾ centimeter should get about 1–2 minutes per side.
#Serve immediately, with lemon and (optionally) bread.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The best and most traditional cheese to use is [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta]], kefalograviera, kasseri, or kefalotyri.

ingredients_original: 1 large slice of salty, brined white cheese (e.g. feta, sirene)
steps_original: Heat a small frying pan over medium-high heat.

While the pan heats, cut the cheese into slices of the desired size and thickness. Thicker slices will take longer to melt through and may result in burning, while thinner ones will have less chance to brown.

Optionally, dredge the slices in flour—this will create a darker and slightly crispier crust, but is an optional step as the cheese will acquire a very slight crust on its own by virtue of the oil and high heat. It will also reduce the spitting somewhat.
Add the oil to the hot pan and swirl it around. When the oil shimmers and seems to become more fluid, it is ready. Add the cheese and step back—it will spit due to the brine-water on the cheese.
Flip the cheese after a minute or two. A slice of ¾ centimeter should get about 1–2 minutes per side.
Serve immediately, with lemon and (optionally) bread.
