recipes.title: Oatmeal Stout Brownies
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=About 18–24|time=60 minutes|difficulty=2|image=[[File:oatmealstoutbrownies.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe|Brownies, Oatmeal Stout}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

This recipe, created by Joe Stutler, was a national finalist in the 2006 Cooking With Beer Challenge. The malt and oats in the beer enhance the flavor of the chocolate in these delicious brownies. Not overly cake-ey, not overly fudge-ey, the texture is nicely balanced. They're also decadently chocolate, and surprisingly light (thanks to the eggs). Great with a fruity beer, such as a lambic (Framboise, yum!).

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ¾ cup unsweetened [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa powder]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 6 tablespoons unsalted room temperature [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cut into cubes 
* 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] dark bittersweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ¾ cup white [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], at room temperature 
* 1 ½ cup superfine or granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 ¼ cups (10 ounces) oatmeal stout [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] (room temperature) 
* 1 cup semi-sweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]

* 1 package (8 ounces) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]], softened 
* ⅓ cup superfine or granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] 
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook: Vanilla|vanilla extract]] 
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 375°F. Line a 9 x 13-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] with nonstick [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] (or grease and flour, or parchment paper…your call).
# In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, and salt until evenly combined. Set aside.
# Melt butter, bittersweet chocolate, and white chocolate chips in a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double-boiler]] over very low heat, stirring constantly until melted. Remove from heat.
# In a large mixing bowl, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] eggs and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add melted chocolate mixture, beating until combined.
# Beat reserved flour mixture into melted chocolate mixture. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in stout beer. The batter will seem a bit thin. Pour into prepared baking pan. Drop semisweet chocolate chips evenly on top of batter (some will sink in).
# Beat cream cheese in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Gradually beat in sugar. Beat in vanilla and 1 egg just until blended.
# Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie batter in pan; cut through mixture with knife several times for marbled design.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 25–35 minutes on center rack in the oven, until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted in the center comes out almost clean.
# Let brownies cool, uncovered, to room temperature. [[Cookbook:Dusting|Dust]] with confectioners' sugar before serving if desired.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Makes 18 (2x3 inch) to 24 (2x2 inch) brownies. For finger-food/snack portions you could halve these dimensions to get 36–48 brownies.
* Plating suggestion: swirl a raspberry lambic reduction sauce (12 oz lambic reduced to half, 4–6 oz seedless raspberry purée, 2–4 oz turbinado sugar, ½–1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]) on the plate; garnish with [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]], and [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] zest.

recipes.original_wikitext:

steps_original: Cut chicken into sixteen 3x½-inch strips.
Wash and dry mushrooms. Mince the mushrooms until very fine.
Mix flour, ⅔ of the minced mushrooms, salt, black pepper, and a pinch of crumbled rosemary.
Heat a large frying pan with a small amount of oil and a pinch of black pepper.
Roll the chicken strips in the flour mixture and fry.
While the chicken is frying, mix (preferably grind) together the pepper, rosemary, paprika, and salt.
Remove the chicken and set aside.
Deglaze the pan with the wine. Add the spice mix and the remaining mushrooms.
Reduce for a minute or two, then add stock. Reduce to a sauce consistency.

This '''prickly pear soda''' is popular in Mexico and the Southwestern United States. 

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Prickly Pear|prickly pears]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* ½ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Agave Syrup|agave nectar]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]] as needed (see note)

==Procedure==
# Remove the peel from the prickly pears, cut them into small pieces about 0.5 x 0.5 in (1.25 x 1.25 cm), and remove the seeds.
# Combine the fruit flesh, water, and agave nectar in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the mixture until it becomes very thick, then [[Cookbook:Sieve|strain]] it to get approximately 5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (120 ml) of syrup.
# Make the finished soda by combining 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original sparkling water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift, because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Cheese recipes|servings=2|time=10 minutes|difficulty=1|Image=[[File:Welsh Rarebit.jpg|300px]]}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

There is no small amount of disagreement about what constitutes [[w:Welsh Rarebit|Welsh Rarebit]]. Many contend that it is just cheese on toast. At the other end of the spectrum are a variety of recipes in which the bread is steeped in beer or floated in soup. 

It has been said that "Welsh rarebit" is a sort of post Act of Union joke, where Irish Rabbit is just bread, Welsh Rabbit is bread and cheese, Scottish Rabbit is bread and dripping and English Rabbit is actually rabbit. This, however, is a moderately uncontroversial recipe for Welsh Rarebit.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|Dijon mustard]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ teaspoon freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 2 fl oz (60 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] such as porter (Guinness will do)
* 4 fl oz (120 ml) double [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (170 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) grated [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|Cheddar cheese]]
* 4 slices of [[Cookbook:Toast|toast]]

== Procedure ==
# In a medium [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over low heat, melt the butter and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] in the flour. 
# Cook, whisking constantly for 2–3 minutes, being careful not to brown the flour.
# Whisk in mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper until smooth. 
# Add beer and whisk to combine. 
# Pour in cream and whisk until well combined and smooth. 
# Gradually add cheese, stirring constantly, until cheese melts and sauce is smooth; this will take 4–5 minutes.
# Pour over toast and serve immediately.

recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] 

A '''brown betty''' is an American dessert of fruit and bread crumbs. This version uses apples.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] soft [[Cookbook:Bread Crumbs|bread crumbs]]
* ½ cup white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* 3 cups [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] (they don't need to be peeled)
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

== Procedure ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|375°F]].
# [[Cookbook:Sauté|Sauté]] bread crumbs in butter.
# Add apples, cinnamon, sugar, and water.
# If the skillet is oven-proof, cover and place in the oven. If the skillet is not oven-proof, transfer to a greased [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|casserole dish]].
# Cover and [[Cookbook:Bake|bake]] for 30 to 40 minutes, until apples are tender.
# If mixture becomes too dry during baking, add another ¼ cup of water. (Apples vary as to moisture content.)

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Serve with milk or whipped cream.
* If cooking in a [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]], preheat with 15 charcoal briquettes, ⅓ on the bottom, and ⅔ on the top.

Instead of adding milk to tea brewed with water, this method steeps the tea leaves directly in hot milk.

== Ingredients ==
*2 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*2 heaping [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] loose [[Cookbook:Tea Leaves|tea leaves]]

== Equipment ==
*1 medium/small pan (must be at least 5 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] deep)
*[[Cookbook:Sieve|Strainer]]

== Procedure ==
#Pour in the milk into the pan. Let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] on medium-low heat.
#When it is nearly [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]], add the tea.
#Stir it a little with a spatula to allow it to brew before it boils over.
#Take it off the heat when it boils over and pour it into a cup through a strainer.
#Sweeten it with sugar and enjoy!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can get loose tea from any Pakistani and/or Indian store. Some brands are Tapal Danedar, and Lipton.

*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 3.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
*¾ cup (140 g / 5 oz) light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]], packed
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ cup (1 stick / 125 g / 4.5 oz) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted

*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract

#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] the butter, sugars and salt in a mixing bowl until combined.

recipes.title: Iced Tea
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Beverage recipes|servings=>24 servings|time=~10 minutes|difficulty=1|image=[[Image:NCI iced tea.jpg|220px]]|2-20? Cal}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]]

'''Iced tea''' is a sweetened beverage made from tea and organic acids, and sometimes with flavouring adjuncts. It is popular in hot climates, usually served over ice. Fruit juices such as red or white cranberry, grape, orange, grapefruit and passionfruit can be added in amounts ranging from 10–25%.

==Ingredients==
*3 [[Cookbook:tea|tea]] bags 
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Stevia|stevia]]
*2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Citric acid|citric acid]] crystals (or malic / tartaric / citric blends)
*4 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]

==Procedure==

# Fill a drip coffee maker with cold water and place the tea bags in the basket.
# Place the stevia, acid, and sugar in the pot, and place the pot in the machine.
# Let it run through its cycle, then chill the product. This is a concentrate and will make several litres of iced tea.
# Place some ice in a tall glass and fill 80–90% with cold water. Pour in some iced tea nectar. You may reduce the water and add some fruit juice if desired.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Lemon or lime juice can be used instead of the acid crystals.  This will make a cloudier finished product.  Use about 4 ounces.
*Garnish with cherries, pineapple, lemon, or lime slices.
*Note that this product contains virtually no sugar. While 4 teaspoons are used in the concentrate, it is diluted so much that the amount of sugar in a glass is probably less than ¼ teaspoon. 
*While stevia is fairly expensive, it goes a long way. Use only pure stevia.

==Ingredients==

* 1 pack (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) Hong Kong-style [[Cookbook:Noodle|egg noodles]], rehydrated and boiled if needed
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]

* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

# Heat the oil in a [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] pan, add the garlic, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for about 10 seconds until golden brown.

# Add the cabbage and scallion, and stir fry at least until all ingredients are hot.
# Add the noodles, and stir fry until all ingredients are hot.
# Add the bean sprouts, light soy sauce, salt, sugar and pepper. Mix well and stir fry (perhaps on reduced heat) until all ingredients are hot, taking care to not cook so long as to overly wilt the bean sprouts.

Add the bean sprouts, light soy sauce, salt, sugar and pepper. Mix well and stir fry (perhaps on reduced heat) until all ingredients are hot, taking care to not cook so long as to overly wilt the bean sprouts.
Serve immediately with fried onion.

'''Zuppa toscana'''<!--Not a typo; Italian does not capitalize adjectives derived from proper names.--> is a soup available at the Olive Garden restaurant.

''Sachertorte'' from [[w:Hotel Sacher|Hotel Sacher]], [[w:Vienna|Vienna]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] '''Sachertorte''' (Ger. ˈzɑxər ˈtɔrtə; Eng.ˈsɑkər ˈtɔrt) is a chocolate cake, invented by Franz Sacher in 1832 for Klemens Wenzel von Metternich in Vienna, Austria. It is one of the most famous Viennese culinary specialties. The cake consists of two layers of dense, not overly sweet chocolate cake with a thin layer of apricot jam in the middle and dark chocolate icing with shreds of chocolate on the top and sides. This is traditionally eaten with whipped cream, as most Viennese consider the Sachertorte too "dry" to be eaten without. The trademark for the "Original Sachertorte" was registered by the [[w:Hotel Sacher|Hotel Sacher]], which was built in 1876 by the son of Franz Sacher. The original recipe is a well-kept secret. == Ingredients == * 6 [[cookbook:egg|eggs]], [[cookbook:Separating Eggs|separated]] * ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) white [[cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]] * 1 cup (240 ml) [[cookbook:flour|flour]] * 1 cup (240 ml) [[cookbook:Confectioners sugar|confectioner's sugar]] * 9 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] (135 ml) [[cookbook:butter|butter]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] (4 ml) [[cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]] * 4 ½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (130 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[cookbook:Dark chocolate|dark chocolate]] == Procedure == # Butter a 9 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]] (22 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) pan and line bottom with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]]. Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|325°F (163°C or Gas Mark 3)]]. # Melt chocolate in [[cookbook:Microwave Oven|microwave]], remove, and let cool, while stirring often. # [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] butter in mixer, then, on low, add confectioners sugar. Return to high, beat for 2 more minutes, beat in [[cookbook:Egg yolk|egg yolk]]s one at a time, then add chocolate and vanilla. # [[cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] [[cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]] and granulated sugar together in a bowl. Stir 1 quarter of it into the chocolate mix, then [[cookbook:fold|fold]] in the rest. # [[cookbook:Sift|Sift]] half the flour into mixture, [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] in, and repeat with remaining flour. # Spread evenly in pan, then [[cookbook:bake|bake]] for about 45 minutes. # Let cool 10 minutes, then remove from pan. # Glaze and frost cake to your liking. == Notes, tips, and variations == *[[The Original Sacher Torte]] *[[Cookbook:Sachertorte (Duramecho version)|Sachertorte (Duramecho version)]] *Glaze the cake with ½ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Apricot|apricot]] jam, either on the top or between two layers of cake (split the cake in two with a long knife) *Sample frosting: Melt 9 oz (260 g) dark chocolate with 2 oz (60 g) butter at low heat and let it cool off a bit. With a spatula, spread over the cake. ingredients_original: ½ cup (120 ml) white granulated sugar
steps_original: Butter a 9 in (22 cm) pan and line bottom with parchment paper. Preheat oven to 325°F (163°C or Gas Mark 3).
Melt chocolate in microwave, remove, and let cool, while stirring often.
Beat butter in mixer, then, on low, add confectioners sugar. Return to high, beat for 2 more minutes, beat in egg yolks one at a time, then add chocolate and vanilla.
Whisk egg whites and granulated sugar together in a bowl. Stir 1 quarter of it into the chocolate mix, then fold in the rest.
Sift half the flour into mixture, fold in, and repeat with remaining flour.
Spread evenly in pan, then bake for about 45 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes, then remove from pan.
Glaze and frost cake to your liking.

'''Vietnamese fish sauce''' is a dipping sauce prepared for use at the table. It contains a more concentrated fish sauce of a similar name.  

==Ingredients==
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|nước mắm (concentrated fish sauce)]]
*1½ cups water
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] or about 2 cloves pressed through a garlic press
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|sambal oelek]] (a type of hot chile sauce)

==Procedure==
#Mix all ingredients together.
#If desired, bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] that cannot be stirred down.
#Cover and refrigerate.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*In restaurants it is served in small bowls, one for each diner, often with a bit of [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]] on top. It is sometimes served with rolls of various types (summer rolls, spring rolls, Imperial rolls, etc.) and is usually available in Vietnamese restaurants upon request.
*For home use, some prefer to store it in a squirt bottle and grind the sambal oelek and garlic to a smaller size using a mortar and pestle so that they do not clog the nozzle.
*You may find the smell quite strong in making this, especially if you decide to boil. Persevere.
*The Three Crabs Brand of concentrated fish sauce is universally praised. There are many, many other brands.

recipes.title: Egg Noodles I
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| Category = Pasta recipes
| Servings = 12–16
| Time = 1 hour prep, 5 minutes cook
| Rating = 3
}}{{Recipe}}

These homemade noodles can be served with a variety of pasta sauces, such as [[Cookbook:Pesto|pesto]] sauce.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 whole [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* ⅛ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* 3 cups (700 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]

== Procedure ==
# In a bowl [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] together eggs, salt, olive oil, and wine.
# Stir in 1 cup flour with fork.
# Gently add second cup of flour after the first is mixed thoroughly.
# Remove mixture from bowl and place on a lightly floured work surface.
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] in the last cup of flour a bit at a time. If the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] becomes too dry, add a bit of cold [[Cookbook:Water|water]].
# Continue kneading until the dough is uniform and shiny in appearance.
# Roll into a large ball and cut into quarters. Overturn the mixing bowl over the cut pieces to protect from dust and drying out.
# Let dough relax for approx. 30 minutes.
# Shape noodles as desired (see notes).
# To cook, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a rolling boil. Add rolled and cut noodles to the water and cook to al dente.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* This dough can be rolled and used for lasagna, cut and used for fettuccine, or rolled out for ravioli. One quarter cut into fettuccine will feed four.
* Store any remaining dough lightly floured in a bag in the refrigerator for up to two weeks, or dried and stored in a cool dry place for up to a month.
* Generally speaking, 1 small egg to 1 cup of flour is what is expected. For a lean dough, increase the flour to egg ratio (you really can't go too far; the poor use no egg at all). For a rich dough omit the egg whites and use 2–3 yolks per cup of flour.
* '''When Kneading:''' It may get tough to knead the flour into the dough when you are down to the last ¼ cup (60 g). Be careful not to add too much water to the dough after you have begun kneading. Lightly dipping your fingers into the water and coating the outside of the dough should be enough. Kneading is hard work and it takes the better part of 20 minutes for proper consistency. If you have the time, bring the dough together in a shaggy ball and allow it to sit tightly wrapped in [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]] overnight in refrigerator; this will allow the gluten to fully hydrate, alleviating some of the time and work of the kneading job.
* '''To Store:''' In order to prevent sticking it is helpful to [[Cookbook:Blanching|blanch]] the pasta for a second or two in boiling salted water, then air dry on a sheet. Finally, dust the noodles with rice flour or corn starch to store. Refrigerate for 5–7 days, or freeze for 6 months to a year.
* '''Non-Alcoholic Variation:''' ½ cup (120ml) of [[Cookbook:Water|water]] can be used in place of the [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]

A recipe for a vegan mayonnaise substitute using tofu and olive oil.

==Ingredients==
*6 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]] [[cookbook:tofu|tofu]] (silky or soft preferred)
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

==Procedure==

recipes.title: Creamy Tomato and Bean Soup
recipes.original_wikitext:
__notoc__
{{recipesummary
| category = Soup recipes
| servings = 8
| time = 45 minutes
| difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

This recipe for '''creamy tomato bean soup''' uses mostly canned ingredients which means that it is faster to prepare than if using fresh tomatoes and dry beans. This [[Cookbook:blend|blended]] soup is [[cookbook:vegetarian|vegetarian]] and hearty enough to be eaten as a main course in a meal. This soup can also be made [[cookbook:vegan|vegan]] by omitting the cream cheese.

==Ingredients==
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]] or [[Cookbook:oil|neutral cooking oil]]
* 1 medium yellow [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], roughly [[Cookbook:chop|chopped]]
* [[cookbook:salt|Salt]] and [[cookbook:black pepper|pepper]] to taste
* 1 can (15 [[Cookbook:ounce|oz]] / 425 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Common Bean|white beans]], with liquid
* 5–10 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]] (according to preference), peeled and cut in half
* ½ tsp dried [[Cookbook:oregano|oregano]]
* 2 leaves fresh [[Cookbook:sage|sage]], torn in half by hand
* 2 cans (30 oz / 850 g) crushed or diced [[Cookbook:tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 can (6 oz / 170 g) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:crushed red pepper|crushed red pepper]]
* 1 [[cookbook:cup|cup]] (237 [[cookbook:milliliter|ml]]) water
* 8 oz (225 g) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* 10–20 leaves of fresh [[cookbook:basil|basil]], [[Cookbook:chiffonade|chiffonaded]] or torn to strips by hand

==Special equipment==
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]

==Procedure==
# Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat for about 30 seconds or until it begins to shimmer.
# Add onions to the large pot of oil, and season with salt and pepper. Cook about 2 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
# Add the beans with their liquid, garlic, oregano, and sage. [[cookbook:simmer|Simmer]] for 3–5 minutes.
# Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, red pepper, and water. Simmer an additional 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Remove from heat, stir in the cream cheese. and break up any large piece with the stirring utensil.
# Let the soup cool for 1–2 minutes, then use either a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] or stick blender to [[cookbook:purée|purée]] the soup.
# Return the puréed soup to the stove at the lowest heat setting for an additional 10–15 minutes, stirring often to prevent burning.
# Just before serving, stir in fresh basil leaves, reserving a handful to [[Cookbook:garnish|garnish]] each bowl.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Be sure to add the basil at the end as it loses flavor during cooking.
* Many types of white bean will work, such as navy, great northern, or cannellini.

recipes.original_wikitext:
__notoc__
{{Recipe}}

{{recipesummary

}}'''Baklava''' is a Mediterranean dessert consisting of layers of phyllo dough interspersed with crushed nuts and soaked in sweet syrup. 

This recipe is modified from one at Allrecipes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baklava |url=https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/9454/greek-baklava/ |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Allrecipes |language=en}}</ref> 

== Ingredients ==

* 1 lb (450 g) [[Cookbook:Nuts and Seeds|nuts]] (any type, but preferrably [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]] or [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (5 ml) ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo dough]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1 tsp (5 ml) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
* ⅓ cup (80 ml) [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* ⅔ cup (160 ml) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* ¾ cup (180 ml) water

== Procedure ==

# Combine the nuts and cinnamon in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]. Blend the nuts into a fine powder, being careful not to form a paste. 
# Melt the butter in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium heat, then set aside.
# Line a [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]].
# Count the number of sheets of phyllo dough and divide it by eight. Arrange one-eighth of the sheets in the bottom of the pan, on the parchment paper.
# Divide the chopped nuts into seven equally sized portions.
# Brush the phyllo dough with melted butter, and evenly distribute one portion of chopped nuts over the dough.
# Arrange another eighth of the phyllo sheets on top of the nut layer.
# Repeat the buttering and layering of nuts and phyllo until you have used up all the phyllo sheets and chopped nuts.
# Using a sharp knife, radially cut the baklava into eight equally sized portions shaped like the British flag.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the baklava for 25 minutes at 350°F (180°C). Remove from the oven, and let cool slightly.
# Mix the vanilla extract, honey, sugar, and water in a clean saucepan. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] over medium heat until it becomes a very thick and viscous syrup of slightly over 1 cup (240 ml). Remove from the heat, and let cool slightly. 
# Pour the syrup on top of the baked baklava, coating each portion of the baklava evenly with syrup.
# Let everything cool fully before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Do not pour the syrup until both the baklava and the syrup are cool to avoid burns.

ingredients_original: 1 lb (450 g) nuts (any type, but preferrably pistachios or walnuts)
steps_original: Combine the nuts and cinnamon in a blender. Blend the nuts into a fine powder, being careful not to form a paste.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then set aside.
Line a baking pan with parchment paper.
Count the number of sheets of phyllo dough and divide it by eight. Arrange one-eighth of the sheets in the bottom of the pan, on the parchment paper.
Divide the chopped nuts into seven equally sized portions.
Brush the phyllo dough with melted butter, and evenly distribute one portion of chopped nuts over the dough.
Arrange another eighth of the phyllo sheets on top of the nut layer.
Repeat the buttering and layering of nuts and phyllo until you have used up all the phyllo sheets and chopped nuts.
Using a sharp knife, radially cut the baklava into eight equally sized portions shaped like the British flag.
Bake the baklava for 25 minutes at 350°F (180°C). Remove from the oven, and let cool slightly.

Mix the vanilla extract, honey, sugar, and water in a clean saucepan. Boil over medium heat until it becomes a very thick and viscous syrup of slightly over 1 cup (240 ml). Remove from the heat, and let cool slightly.
Pour the syrup on top of the baked baklava, coating each portion of the baklava evenly with syrup.
Let everything cool fully before serving.

recipes.title: Socca (Italian Chickpea Flatbread)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary
| Category = French recipes
| Time = 15–30 minutes
| Servings = 16 (or 8, twice!)
| Rating = 1
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[Image:Socca.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Cuisine of Italy]]

'''Socca''' (French), '''torta di ceci''' or '''farinata''' (Italian), is a type of [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] made from chickpea flour.

''See also: [[Cookbook:Calentita|Calentita]]''

==Ingredients==

* 300 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Chickpea Flour|chickpea flour]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 cups) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]] to taste; 2–3 decent grinds of a grinder should do

==Equipment==

* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]
* Something to cook the ''socca'' on; traditionally, a 50cm (20 inch) copper plaque is used as it spreads the heat evenly to all parts of the ''socca'', but a good [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|cast iron pan]] will suffice if preheated in the oven first. 

==Procedure==
# Heat oven as high as it can go—around 300°C / 570°F is traditional, but do whatever your oven can manage that gets close to this. If using a cast-iron pan, get it into the oven at the start so that it is hot when the batter goes into it.
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] all the ingredients together well, ensuring there are no lumps. This should make a very thin, easy-to-pour batter.
# Once the oven is up to temperature, pour some of the batter into the hot pan or onto the plaque, and put into the oven for 8–9 minutes at 300°C / 570°F, or 13–15 minutes at 250°C / 480°F. With a 50 cm plaque or pan, cook half the batter at a time—the batter should cover the plaque or pan very thinly.
# Remove from the oven and cut into triangular wedges. Serve hot.
# Repeat for the rest of the batter.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Asian recipes|servings=4|time=½ hour|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]]

==Ingredients==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Garlic|cloves garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|fresh ginger root]]
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Chile|fresh hot chiles]], minced (or ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Red Pepper|hot red pepper flakes]])
* 4 [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallions]], separated: white part minced, green part cut on the diagonal in ½-inch pieces
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Douchi|Chinese black beans]]
* ¼ to ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Wine|rice wine]] or [[Cookbook:Wine|sherry]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (900 g) [[Cookbook:Shellfish|shellfish]] ([[Cookbook:Clam|clams]], [[Cookbook:Mussel|mussels]], [[Cookbook:Crab|crabs]], and/or [[Cookbook:Lobster|lobster]]) or 1 pound (450 g) of [[Cookbook:shrimp|shrimp]], [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], [[Cookbook:Poultry|poultry]], or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* 1½ tablespoons [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Onion|onion cubes]]
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]] or ½ red and ½ [[Cookbook:Green Pepper|green peppers]], cut in cubes
* 2–3 cups, thinly sliced [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]] ([[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], [[Cookbook:Snow Pea|snow peas]], and/or [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* [[Cookbook:Steaming|Steamed]] [[Cookbook:Rice|white rice]], optional

==Procedure==
# In small bowl, combine garlic, ginger root, chilies, scallion whites, and black beans.
# In another small bowl, combine ¼ cup stock, soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil, and stir until sugar dissolves.
# In a third small bowl, dissolve cornstarch in wine or sherry.
# Scrub clams, if using, cut shellfish into 1-inch pieces or thinly slice poultry or meat.
# Just before serving, heat a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] over high heat.
# Swirl in canola oil.
# [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|Stir-Fry]] onion and bell pepper for a minute then add garlic and bean mixture and cook for 15 seconds, or until fragrant but not brown.
# Add seafood and stir-fry for 1 minute.
# Add stock-based sauce and cook for 2 to 5 minutes, or until seafood is cooked; if necessary to prevent mixture from sticking to pan, add remaining stock. (If steaming clams, tightly cover wok.)
# Stir cornstarch mixture and add to stir-fry along with scallion greens and sliced vegetables.
# Bring sauce to a [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]].
# Serve immediately along with white rice if desired.

recipes.title: Potato-Almond Milk
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Beverage recipes|servings=4–6|time=1 hour 20 minutes|difficulty=1
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Potato milk''' is an alternative non-dairy drink that can be used instead of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]].

== Ingredients ==

* 40 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
* 2 large white [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]] or [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* ½ tsp salt
* 600 ml water

== Equipment ==

* Chopping board 
* [[Cookbook:Peeler|Peeler]]
* Large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]
* Large knife 
* Measuring jug 
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]
* Double-layer of [[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|cheesecloth]] or nut-milk bag
== Procedure ==

# Pre-soak your almonds in water for 1 hour and then drain.
# Cut potatoes 5 cm chunks. Place the chunks into saucepan with enough water to fully cover them.
# Bring the saucepan to a [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmer]] over high heat, and simmer for around 15 minutes until tender. 
# Drain the potatoes. Transfer to blender with the almonds, vanilla, maple syrup, and salt. Add the water, and blend until smooth on a high speed, adding more water as necessary.
# Stretch the cheesecloth over a large bowl, and pour your mixture into it. Use a fork to agitate as needed, and let the milk drain through.
# When strained, taste the milk. Adjust by adding more water, vanilla, salt, or maple syrup as needed, depending on your taste.
# Chill and serve, shaking the mixture beforehand.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can reuse any leftover potato mixture in other dishes, like potato scones or mashed potato.
* A fine metal strainer can be used in place of the cheesecloth, although it's not as effective in removing the finer particles.

The recipe utilizes baking in foil, which is a great low-fat cooking method that produces wonderfully tender and juicy chicken. ==Ingredients== *4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] fresh [[Cookbook:Dill|dill]] *4 [[cookbook:tsp|tsp]] grated [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]] peel *3 [[cookbook:tsp|tsp]] minced [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] *¾ [[cookbook:tsp|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] *4 [[cookbook:cup|cup]] cherry [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], halved *1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] *4 skinless boneless [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breast halves, thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] crosswise *4 [[cookbook:cup|cups]] firmly packed torn fresh [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] leaves (about 8 ounces) ==Equipment and supplies== *Large [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] *Medium bowl *Small bowl *[[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]] ==Procedure== #Preheat oven to 400°F. #Place large baking sheet in oven to heat. #Mix dill, orange peel, garlic and salt in medium bowl. Season with pepper. #Combine tomatoes, oil and 1 teaspoon dill mixture in small bowl. #Add chicken to remaining dill mixture in medium bowl and [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] to coat. #Cut 4 sheets of foil each about 20 inches long. #Arrange 1 cup spinach on 1 sheet of foil. #Place a quarter of the sliced chicken mixture atop spinach. #Spoon a quarter of the tomato mixture atop chicken. #Fold foil over, enclosing contents completely and crimping edges tightly to seal. #Repeat with remaining 3 foil sheets, forming 4 packets total. #Arrange foil packets in single layer on heated baking sheet. #[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until chicken is just cooked through, about 15 minutes. #Transfer to plates; let stand 5 minutes. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *Serve with rice. ==References==

ingredients_original: 4 skinless boneless chicken breast halves, thinly sliced crosswise
4 cups firmly packed torn fresh spinach leaves (about 8 ounces)
steps_original: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place large baking sheet in oven to heat.
Mix dill, orange peel, garlic and salt in medium bowl. Season with pepper.
Combine tomatoes, oil and 1 teaspoon dill mixture in small bowl.
Add chicken to remaining dill mixture in medium bowl and toss to coat.
Cut 4 sheets of foil each about 20 inches long.
Arrange 1 cup spinach on 1 sheet of foil.
Place a quarter of the sliced chicken mixture atop spinach.
Spoon a quarter of the tomato mixture atop chicken.
Fold foil over, enclosing contents completely and crimping edges tightly to seal.
Repeat with remaining 3 foil sheets, forming 4 packets total.
Arrange foil packets in single layer on heated baking sheet.
Bake until chicken is just cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Transfer to plates; let stand 5 minutes.
recipes.notes_source_wikitext: *Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Summer Pudding
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=1–2 hours|difficulty=2
| Image = [[File:Summer pudding.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Summer pudding''' is a quintessentially British [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] made from wonderful fresh ingredients only available in the summer months. It is redolent of a private dinner at a smart country house, maybe somewhere in the Surrey hills near Shere, with the taste of an exquisite first course still lingering, a bottle of chilled champagne still half full, and the prospect of more enticing conversation to come as the evening turns into night. Once you make it once, you'll make it again and again!

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Punnet|punnet]] [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]], large ones halved
* 1 punnet [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]]
* ½ punnet [[Cookbook:Currant|blackcurrants]]
* ½ punnet [[Cookbook:Currant|redcurrants]]
* 1 loaf of white, pappy sort of [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] or [[Cookbook:Brioche|brioche]], crusts removed and sliced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Caster sugar|caster sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]], finely [[Cookbook:Zest|zested]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 bottle of the best quality blackcurrant cordial you can find, in reserve

== Procedure ==

# Liberally butter the inside a pudding bowl about 5 inches in diameter. The bowl should preferably not be greater in diameter that the size of your pieces of sliced bread. If you are worried about getting the whole thing out of the bowl in one piece, line the bowl first with some [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|cling film]]. It's a fiddly job, but ensures you get a perfect shape at the end.
# Combine the blackcurrants, redcurrants, mint leaves, lime zest, sugar, and about 3 tbsp water. [[Cookbook:Poaching|Poach]] them for about 5 minutes on the lowest possible heat setting of your stove. Add the strawberries and poach for another minute.
# Turn the heat off and add the raspberries. Leave to cool.
# Using the prepared bowl as a guide, cut a circle out of the white bread the same diameter as the top of the bowl. Do the same with the bottom of the bowl.
# Using a sharp knife, slice the bread into squares or oblongs, roughly the same height as the bowl, which will be used to line the inside of the bowl. This does not have to be an exact science. In simple terms what we are trying to do is to line the bowl with the white bread.
# Lay the smaller circle of white bread on the bottom of the bowl. Put the oblongs of white bread up the side of the bowl, overlapping slightly, and pour the fruit mixture into the void right up to the top. The bread should become well soaked in the juice from the cooked fruit. Indeed if there is not enough juice to soak the bread so it turns very red, use the cordial as a top-up.
# Place the large circle, or disc, of bread on the top and press it down well.
# Top with a weight or something that fits into the top of the bowl so it squashes everything down tight, and place it in the fridge for at least 40 minutes.
# When you are ready to serve the pudding, carefully using a knife to release the bread mould from the side of the bowl, and invert the whole thing onto a plate. If things become a little fraught and wobbly at this point, don't panic—just sort of whack everything back into shape using a wooden spoon.
# Decorate your plate with some more summer fruit, maybe a couple of mint leaves, and an artistic dollop of fresh [[Cookbook:Whipped Cream|whipped cream]] or [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], then serve with a flourish.

1 bottle of the best quality blackcurrant cordial you can find, in reserve
steps_original: Liberally butter the inside a pudding bowl about 5 inches in diameter. The bowl should preferably not be greater in diameter that the size of your pieces of sliced bread. If you are worried about getting the whole thing out of the bowl in one piece, line the bowl first with some cling film. It's a fiddly job, but ensures you get a perfect shape at the end.

Combine the blackcurrants, redcurrants, mint leaves, lime zest, sugar, and about 3 tbsp water. Poach them for about 5 minutes on the lowest possible heat setting of your stove. Add the strawberries and poach for another minute.
Turn the heat off and add the raspberries. Leave to cool.
Using the prepared bowl as a guide, cut a circle out of the white bread the same diameter as the top of the bowl. Do the same with the bottom of the bowl.

Using a sharp knife, slice the bread into squares or oblongs, roughly the same height as the bowl, which will be used to line the inside of the bowl. This does not have to be an exact science. In simple terms what we are trying to do is to line the bowl with the white bread.

Lay the smaller circle of white bread on the bottom of the bowl. Put the oblongs of white bread up the side of the bowl, overlapping slightly, and pour the fruit mixture into the void right up to the top. The bread should become well soaked in the juice from the cooked fruit. Indeed if there is not enough juice to soak the bread so it turns very red, use the cordial as a top-up.
Place the large circle, or disc, of bread on the top and press it down well.
Top with a weight or something that fits into the top of the bowl so it squashes everything down tight, and place it in the fridge for at least 40 minutes.

When you are ready to serve the pudding, carefully using a knife to release the bread mould from the side of the bowl, and invert the whole thing onto a plate. If things become a little fraught and wobbly at this point, don't panic—just sort of whack everything back into shape using a wooden spoon.
Decorate your plate with some more summer fruit, maybe a couple of mint leaves, and an artistic dollop of fresh whipped cream or crème fraîche, then serve with a flourish.

This '''chicken bacon broccoli alfredo spaghetti''' recipe is adapted from the YouTube channel Tasty.<ref>https://google.miraheze.org/wiki/YouTube_Wiki:8_Scrumptious_Spaghetti_Recipes_•_Tasty</ref>

== Ingredients ==

#[[Cookbook:Boiling Pasta|Boil]] the spaghetti in water until ''[[Cookbook:Al Dente|al dente]]''.

recipes.title: Potato Curry (Aloo Masala)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Side dish recipes|servings=4-6|time=20 minutes|difficulty=3|Image=[[File:An Aesthetic Potato Masala.jpg|300px]]}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan]]

'''Potato masala''' (Tamil: ''uralai kizhangu masala'') is a potato dish often served alongside [[Cookbook:Roti|roti]] or folded inside a [[Cookbook:Dosa|dosa]]. The dosa and aloo masala combination, widely eaten in South [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]], is known as ''masala dosa''. [[Cookbook:Coconut Chutney|Coconut chutney]] is a common accompaniment.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[cookbook:oil|oil]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Mustard Seed|mustard seed]]
* ½ tablespoon [[Cookbook:Chickpea|chana]] [[Cookbook:Dal|dhal]] (optional)
* 5 [[Cookbook:Curry Leaf|curry leaves]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], chopped thin
* 4-5 split green [[Cookbook:Chilli pepper|chillies]]
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], cubed and par-boiled
* 1 pinch of [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
==Procedure==
# Heat oil.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sautée]] the mustard seed first, then add chana dhal, curry leaves, onion and chillies. 
# Fry until the onions begin to change color.
# Add potatoes.
# Sprinkle the turmeric evenly and stir well to mix all the ingredients
# Cover and cook on a medium flame for about 5 minutes, stirring well, until the potatoes become very soft and somewhat mashed.
# Season with salt to taste.

recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Potato recipes|servings=4–5 people|time=90 minutes|difficulty=2
| image = [[File:Three bowls of potato soup.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Soup|Soup]]

==Ingredients==
*6 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*3 cups water
*2 cubes [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|chicken bouillon]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to taste
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
*1 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*¼ tsp dried [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]

==Procedure==
#Cook onion in butter until tender.
#Bring the diced potatoes, carrots, water and chicken bouillon in another stock pot to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] about 10 minutes or until tender. Add ground black pepper.
#Add the flour to the cooked onions to make a paste. Stir in the milk. Cook over low heat stirring constantly until warmed through. Add the potato and carrot mixture. Stir in the parsley and thyme and heat through. Serve hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Use vegetable [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] instead of chicken bouillon for a vegetarian soup.
*Add [[Cookbook:Leek|leeks]] if available.
*Omit all ingredients except potatoes, water, salt and pepper for a simple and surprisingly pleasing potato soup. High quality, flavorful potatoes are required for this variation, which itself presents an ideal base for an inventive cook to expand upon.

'''Butter tea''', known as ''Po Cha'', is a traditional drink of the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Tibet|Tibetans]] and is also consumed in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Bhutan|Bhutan]]. Butter tea is an indispensable part of Tibetan life. Before work, a Tibetan will down several bowlfuls of this tangy beverage, and it is always served to guests. Since butter is the main ingredient, butter tea is a very warming drink and a good antidote to the cold, so it is especially suited to high altitudes. 

According to the Tibetan custom, butter tea is drunk in separate sips, and after each sip the host refills the bowl to the brim. Thus the guest never drains his bowl yet it is constantly topped up. If the visitor does not wish to drink, the best thing to do is leave the tea untouched until the time comes to leave and then drain the bowl. In this way etiquette is observed and the host will not be offended.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] regular [[Cookbook:Tea Leaf|black tea leaves]] (preferably [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Nepal|Nepalese]] or [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]])
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (or 1½ cup [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half-and-half]] + 1½ cup water)
* 2 tablespoons unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure == 
# Boil tea with milk for 2–10 minutes, depending upon the strength of tea desired
# Strain into tea cups. 
# Add butter and salt. Stir thoroughly, ideally by carefully using a blender, and serve.

'''Buckeyes''' are an easy snack named from their resemblance to the nut of the Buckeye tree.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (320 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/11 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:butter|melted butter]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:vanilla|vanilla]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] ({{convert|375|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]]
* 1 small bag ({{convert|100|g|oz|abbr=on|disp=s}}) [[Cookbook:Chocolate chip|semi-sweet chocolate chips]]
* 25 [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpicks]]

==Procedure==
#Mix peanut butter, melted butter, vanilla, and powdered sugar in a bowl.
#Form the mixture into 1-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] balls.
#Place a toothpick into each ball.
#Refrigerate or freeze for an hour.
#Melt the semi-sweet chocolate chips in a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]].
#Dip the balls in the melted chocolate, leaving a small exposed circle at the top.
#Place on wax paper and remove toothpick.
#Refrigerate or freeze.

Dip the balls in the melted chocolate, leaving a small exposed circle at the top.
Place on wax paper and remove toothpick.
Refrigerate or freeze.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Bread II
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Cake recipes|servings=16|time=1 hour|difficulty=3
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Midwestern cuisine|Midwestern cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday Recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]
* 1 can (15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:pumpkin|pumpkin]] [[Cookbook:Puree|purée]]
* 3 cups white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 3½ cups [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Allspice|ground allspice]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]]
* 1½ teaspoons [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] raw pumpkin seeds, for [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat oven to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|375°F]].
# Butter and lightly flour 2 medium [[Cookbook:Loaf Pan|loaf pans]] (8 ½ by 4 ½ by 2 ½ inches).
# Using a [[Cookbook:Mixer|stand mixer]] fitted with the paddle attachment, combine eggs, oil, pumpkin and sugar until smooth.
# In a separate bowl, combine the flour, soda, salt, allspice, cinnamon and nutmeg.
# With the machine on low speed, add the flour mixture to the pumpkin mixture in ¼-cup increments.
# Scrape down the side of the bowl and mix for another 30 seconds or so, until all ingredients are well-combined.
# Divide the mixture equally between the 2 loaf pans.
# Sprinkle the top of each loaf with 1 tablespoon pumpkin seeds.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] 40–45 minutes until a tester inserted into the center of each loaf comes out clean.
# Allow loaves to cool in the pans for 5–10 minutes before unmolding, then allow loaves to cool on a wire rack to room temperature before cutting or wrapping.

recipes.title: Baingan Bartha (South Indian Eggplant with Coconut and Chili) I
recipes.source_title: Cookbook:Baingan Bartha (South Indian Eggplant with Coconut and Chili) I
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Indian recipes|servings=4|time=40 minutes|difficulty=2|Image=[[File:Baigan ( Brinjal ) Bharta.jpg|300px]]}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian]]

'''Baingan bartha''' is an [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant (aubergine)]] dish much loved all over [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]]. This southern version of the dish is very different from northern varieties, and well suited to the cuisine of the region.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] / 450 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant (aubergine)]]
* 2–6 green [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chillies]], as desired
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] fresh ground [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
* 1 [[Cookbook :Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves (cilantro)]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]] or [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Roast the eggplant directly over a low flame. Don't be afraid to set it right on the gas burner, turning it regularly until the skin becomes blackened and brittle and the flesh soft (about 15–20 minutes).
# Set aside to cool.
# Grind the chillies, coconut, and coriander together in a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] to form a paste.
# Peel the eggplant skin off and mash the flesh to a uniform pulp by hand.
# Mix in the coconut paste and paneer/yogurt, along with salt to taste.
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Chapati|chapatis]], [[Cookbook:Dosa|dosa]] or [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Baingan bartha is commonly produced with [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]] (seeds) and/or [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] (leaves, from the same plant, and thus sometimes confusingly called coriander as well).

recipes.title: Red Cross Fudge
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Confection recipes
| Yield = 4 pounds (1.8 kg)|servings=~80|time=20 minutes plus cooling|difficulty=2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Confections|Confections]]

'''Red cross fudge''' is a delicious, easy fudge that works every time and never crystallizes.

== Ingredients ==
* 4½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] / 2.2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* {{convert|0.5|lb|g}} [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1½ cups (375 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 12.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Condensed Milk|evaporated milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* 2 cups (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.2 oz) miniature [[Cookbook:Marshmallow|marshmallows]]
* 12 oz (340 g) real [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate chips]]
* 2 cups (120 g / 4.2 oz) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine sugar, butter, evaporated milk, and vanilla in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and bring to a rolling [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Cook on medium heat for 11 minutes, stirring constantly.
# Add marshmallows, chocolate chips, walnuts to fudge and mix well.
# Pour into a buttered pan and let cool. 
# Cut into squares when it cuts without melting back together but before it becomes crumbly. 
# Store in an air-tight container.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Substituting margarine for butter makes the fudge oily. Imitation vanilla affects the aroma.
* Other varieties of chips (vanilla, butterscotch, etc.) work as well.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook: Flatbread|Flatbread]]

'''North American pancakes''' are a type of [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancake]] prepared from a [[Cookbook: Batter|batter]] that is baked on a hot griddle or frying pan. They exist in several variations in many different local [[Cookbook: Cuisine|cuisines]].

== Ingredients ==
* 120 [[Cookbook: Gram|g]] (½ [[Cookbook: Cup|cup]] or 4 [[Cookbook: Ounce|oz]]) wheat [[Cookbook: Flour|flour]] (white, whole grain or 1:1 mix of white and whole grain)
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook: Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook: Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook: Salt|salt]]
* 250 [[Cookbook: Milliliter|ml]] (1 cup or 8 [[Cookbook: Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook: Milk|milk]] (substitute [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] or 1:1 mix of milk and buttermilk)
* 1 [[Cookbook: Eggs|egg]], [[Cookbook: Separate|separated]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook: White sugar|white sugar]] (optional; this will add a sweetness to your pancakes and is recommended if you are not using any sauces, syrups or ingredient such as bananas or blueberries that will add natural sugars to the mix)

== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, mix dry ingredients together until well-blended.
# Add milk and mix well until smooth.
# [[Cookbook: Separate|Separate]] the egg, placing the whites in a medium bowl and the yolks in the batter. Mix batter well.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] whites until stiff and then [[Cookbook: Fold|fold]] into batter gently (skip this step for heavier pancakes or if 1 cup buttermilk is substituted for milk).
# Pour ladles of the mixture into a non-stick [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]], one at a time.
# Cook until the edges are dry and bubbles appear on surface. Flip, then cook until golden.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Serve with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]], fruit, chocolate spread, melted [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]], or [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]].
* Many variations of this recipe use a whole [[Cookbook: Beaten egg|beaten egg]] instead of the yolk and whipped whites. In these variations, all wet ingredients are mixed together with the dry ingredients to make the batter before moving on to the cooking.
* Use [[Cookbook: Buttermilk|buttermilk]] or yogurt instead of milk, or wholegrain flours instead of white. This will change the consistency of the final product—whole grain flours generally lead to a denser heavier pancake, so try mixing white and wheat in various proportions as suggested above to get the feel you want.
* Try adding sliced fruit such as [[Cookbook: Banana|banana]] and [[Cookbook: Apple|apple]], or broken crispy bacon to the batter after pouring into the skillet and before flipping.

'''Eärgon salsa''' is an easy-to-make, low sodium hot sauce that nicely complements fresh vegetables like broccoli, carrots, and celery. Easy variations using hotter peppers such as seranos and habaneros are given below.

==Ingredients==
* 4 fresh [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño]] peppers
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] distilled white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 can (12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) unsalted tomato paste

==Procedure==
#Slice peppers crosswise to form small rings, and put in a small container.
#Add garlic, vinegar, and tomato paste.
#Stir and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*4 seranno peppers can be substituted for the 4 jalapeños for a spicier sauce.
*To try the habanero version, use 2 finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] habanero peppers and increase tomato paste from 12 oz to 18 oz. Be careful.
* This recipe is easy to customize. Some options include adding spinach, cilantro, black pepper, and chopped onions.
* The peppers, vinegar, and garlic can be combined beforehand and stored in an airtight container in the fridge for several days.
* Can be easily stored in a closed container in refrigerator for a week or ten days.

This salsa is a good source of vitamins and minerals. One serving provides 42% of a day's recommended Vitamin C, 28% of Vitamin A, 18% of Vitamin E, 14% of pyridoxine, 13% of niacin and vitamin K. In terms of minerals, it provides 25% of a day's potassium, 17% of manganese, 16% of copper, and 14% of iron. Additionally, one serving also has 4 grams of both dietary fiber and protein.

==Warnings==

* Be very careful not to touch your eyes, nose, or mouth after chopping or handling the chili peppers—the pain can be intense. Wash your hands thoroughly after handling.

recipes.original_wikitext:

__NOTOC__
A '''Fribourg omelet''' is a mix of eggs, crunchy greens, and ham, with the Swiss canton of Fribourg’s native Gruyère cheese adding an acidic punch to bind the flavors together.
==Ingredients==
*4 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*1 pinch [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 pinch ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*1 pinch ground [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*3 thin slices of [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], cut in small squares
* 1 handful roughly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] fresh [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]]
* 6 thin 8-cm (3-inch)-wide slices of [[Cookbook:Gruyère Cheese|Gruyère cheese]] 

==Equipment==
* [[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stovetop]]
* 30 cm or 12-inch-diameter [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]]
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]<nowiki/>s
==Procedure==
#In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, salt, pepper, milk and nutmeg, until even and glossy.
# Place half the butter in the skillet on medium heat. Swirl the pan to coat evenly with butter.
# Add ham and cook until deep brown.
# Stir in kale for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted but still crunchy. Set aside the ham and greens.
# Add the remainder of the butter to the skillet over low heat.
# Pour egg mixture into the skillet, moving skillet to create a flat, even layer. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
# Scatter the ham and kale evenly over the top of the eggs.
# Lay the Gruyère slices over the open omelet. Heat until the edges of the cheese have melted slightly.
# Gently push the edges of the omelet less than half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
# Use the spatulas to lift half the omelet and fold over the other half. Move the entire omelet carefully onto a plate and serve.

'''French dressing''' is a [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]] dressing commonly used with green salads. It can also be used as a [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]] spread, or many other uses. A commercial version is also called "Catalina Dressing".

Literally "coffee with milk", '''café au lait''' is a drink made of coffee and scalded milk in a ratio of 1:1. It is the staple coffee drink of French Louisiana and is often served in bowls in [[Cookbook:Cajun cuisine|Acadiana]]. 

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] brewed [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] or 1.5–2 cups (350–475 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) cold [[cookbook:Coffee concentrate|coffee concentrate]]
* 4 cups (950 ml) [[cookbook:milk|milk]]
==Procedure==
# If you are using coffee concentrate, add enough hot water to make 4 cups of coffee.
# At the same time, heat the milk over a low to medium heat until scalded. 
# Pour equal amounts of coffee and scalded milk into bowls or cups. 

==Notes, tips, and variations== 
* Steamed milk can be substituted for scalded milk. 
* The milk can be heated in the cups by half filling each cup with milk and [[Cookbook:Microwaving|microwaving]] briefly. A 1,000W microwave oven will heat one half-cup of milk in 50 seconds, two in 60 seconds.

recipes.title: Lamb Sausages and Grilled Potatoes
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipe}}{{recipesummary|category=Sausage recipes|servings=6|time=40 minutes|difficulty=2|}}This is an easy-to-cook family recipe with sausage as the main ingredient.

==Ingredients==
* 12 small [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] or 10 medium sized ones weighing approximately 971g
* 30 ml olive oil, for potatoes
* 3 ml [[Cookbook:salt|iodised salt]]
* 15 ml olive oil, for frying
* 20 g butter
* 8 lamb [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausages]]
* 12 [[Cookbook:Tomato|cherry tomatoes]]
* 200 g [[Cookbook:Romaine lettuce|Romaine lettuce]], washed and cut into smaller pieces

==Equipment==

* Cooking spatula
* [[Cookbook:Grater|Grater]]
* Measuring tools
* Cake pan
* Mandoline (optional)

==Procedure==
# Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
# Rinse the potatoes, and cut into slices 0.5 cm thick using a knife, grater, or mandoline.
# Put the potatoes in the cake tin, and spread them out. Add the 30 ml of olive oil to cover the entire tin and the potatoes. Sprinkle the salt all over the tin and the potatoes. Bake for 25 minutes in the preheated oven.
# Heat the 15 ml olive oil and the butter in a pan over medium heat until the butter melts. Add the sausages, and cook for about 10 minutes on high heat. Turn the sausages occasionally so they fry on all sides. Remove from the heat.
# Toss the lettuce and tomatoes together to make a salad.
# Serve the salad with the baked potatoes and sausages.

recipes.title: Simple Tarragon Quiche
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=French recipes|servings=6|time=75 minutes|difficulty=2|Image=[[Image:Quiche Lorraine.jpg|300px]]}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]]

A '''quiche''' is a [[Cookbook:Baking|baked]], [[Cookbook:Sweeteners|unsweetened]] [[Cookbook:Custard|custard]] [[Cookbook:Dessert#Pies, Tarts|pie]], often made with savory fillings. Originally served in Germany, quiche was adopted by neighboring France and is now considered a traditional French dish. The French (and now English) word ''quiche'' comes from a dialectal form (''Küchle'') of the German word for [[Cookbook:Dessert#Cakes, cupcakes|cake]] (''Kuchen''). Quiche became popular in Britain after World War II and in the United States during the 1960s and 70s.

==Ingredients==
*5 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]s
*1 ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (320 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] (approximately 30% [[Cookbook:Oil and fat|fat]])
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] fresh [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Dash|dash]] ground [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*⅛ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 prepared frozen [[Cookbook:Pie Crust|pie crust]]
*¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) freshly-[[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Swiss Cheese|Swiss cheese]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|375°F]] (190°C).
#Place the eggs, cream, tarragon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]; blend ''as briefly as possible'' until they form a homogeneous mixture.
#In the pie crust, create alternating layers of the shredded cheese and the mixture from the blender until the crust is full.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the quiche for 35–40 minutes; a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] or fork inserted into its middle should come out "clean".
#Remove the quiche from the oven, and let it cool for at least 20 minutes before serving.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Use nutmeg sparingly.
*Fresh tarragon will be better than dried tarragon.
*Placing a very hot pan in under the quiche will give it greater volume.
*Try making quiches with [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sautéed]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]s, sautéed [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]], and shredded sharp [[Cookbook:Cheddar cheese|cheddar cheese]]; feel free to experiment.

==Warnings==
*The quiche mixture may drip over the edge of the pie crust while cooking; place it on a cookie sheet or place foil on the oven rack below it.
*The quiche will continue to cook after it is removed from the oven; be careful not to overcook it or cut it before it has had a chance to set.
*[[Cookbook:Half and Half|Half-and-half]] (cream with approximately 12% fat) can be substituted for regular cream to make this dish less fattening; however, be cautious of using milk because low-fat dairy products curdle more easily.

[[Category:Recipes using egg]]
[[Category:Recipes for pies and tarts]]
[[Category:Vegetarian recipes]]
[[Category:Recipes_with_metric_units]]

[[Category:Recipes using cream]]
[[Category:Recipes for quiche]]

[[fr:Livre de cuisine/Quiche lorraine]]

steps_original: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Place the eggs, cream, tarragon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a blender; blend as briefly as possible until they form a homogeneous mixture.
In the pie crust, create alternating layers of the shredded cheese and the mixture from the blender until the crust is full.
Bake the quiche for 35–40 minutes; a toothpick or fork inserted into its middle should come out "clean".
Remove the quiche from the oven, and let it cool for at least 20 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Tuna Casserole
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Tuna recipes|servings=6|time=45 minutes|difficulty=1}}

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==

*3 cans of [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]] in water
*1 can each of cream of celery soup, cream of chicken soup, and cream of mushroom soup (substitute cream of potato if you don't like mushrooms)
*1 bag of frozen vegetables ([[Cookbook:Pea|peas]], [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], and [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]])
*1 large bag of egg [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]]
*1 can of fried onion rings, 1 packet potato chips, or 1 small packet [[Cookbook:Corn flakes|corn flakes]]

==Procedure==
# Cook egg noodles as directed on package. While boiling water, preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 400°F.
# Drain egg noodles. Mix together all ingredients except fried onion rings. Put in a [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]] or a 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 20 minutes.
# Sprinkle fried onion topping on top of baked casserole. Bake for an additional 3 minutes, or until fried onion is slightly brown.
# Let cool for 5 minutes and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* You can substitute any of the cream soups with the flavor of your choice.
* You can sprinkle with Old Bay or any other seafood seasoning for added taste.

recipes.title: Tarte Tatin
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=8|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (see notes)
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Apple|Golden Delicious apples]], peeled, cored and quartered
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pastry Dough (recipe)|pastry dough recipe]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|400°F]].
# Place sugar, butter and water in a stovetop/oven-safe [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|tarte dish]] over medium-high heat. Cook until mixture becomes golden brown and bubbly.
# Remove from heat and allow mixture to cool to room temperature in the tarte dish.
# When caramel mixture has cooled, arrange the apple quarters on their sides in the mixture.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the pastry dough out to a thickness of about ½ inch and a diameter large enough to cover the tarte dish.
# Place dough on top of the tarte, then trim and discard the edges.
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] tarte for 40 minutes.
# Allow to cool in the tarte dish for 15 minutes before inverting onto a serving platter.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* European-style butter, which has a higher fat content than American butter, is recommended. Most US supermarkets now stock at least one variety of European-style butter, Plugra being one of the most popular brands.

Place sugar, butter and water in a stovetop/oven-safe tarte dish over medium-high heat. Cook until mixture becomes golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from heat and allow mixture to cool to room temperature in the tarte dish.
When caramel mixture has cooled, arrange the apple quarters on their sides in the mixture.
Roll the pastry dough out to a thickness of about ½ inch and a diameter large enough to cover the tarte dish.
Place dough on top of the tarte, then trim and discard the edges.
Bake tarte for 40 minutes.
Allow to cool in the tarte dish for 15 minutes before inverting onto a serving platter.

recipes.source_title: Cookbook:Black Bean Soup and Salsa Verde
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary|category=Soup recipes|servings=4|time=30 minutes|difficulty=2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southwestern cuisine|Southwestern U.S. cuisine]]
==Ingredients==

* 2 cans (840 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 31 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]], drained
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Low-sodium Cooking|low-sodium]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 cup Mexican [[Cookbook:Salsa#Salsa verde|salsa verde]], or to taste
* ¼ cup packed [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro leaves]], plus extra sprigs for garnish (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cumin|ground cumin]]

==Procedure==

# [[Cookbook:Purée|Purée]] all ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] until smooth. 
# Pour into a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]], and bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. 
# Simmer, partially covered and stirring frequently, to blend flavors, 5 or 7 minutes. 
# Serve, [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnishing]] each portion with 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] of tortilla chips, 1 tablespoon of [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]] and optional cilantro sprigs.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Garnishes can include ¼ cup crumbled [[Cookbook:Tortilla Chip|tortilla chips]] and ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]].

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Irish Soda Bread
recipes.original_wikitext:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Bread recipes|servings=12|time=1 hour|difficulty=2
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:North American cuisines|North America]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ireland|Irish cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]]

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole-wheat]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]

== Procedure ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|325°F]] (165°C / gasmark 3).
# Use [[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|cooking spray]] or grease and then lightly flour a 9x5x3-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|baking pan]].
# Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
# Form a cavity in the middle.
# Pour in the buttermilk.
# Mix until just moistened. Too much mixing will make it tough.
# Gently shape the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] to fit pan.
# Cut the top at least three times with a knife.
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] for 65–70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the bread comes out clean.
# Cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]].
# Wrap in tea-towel or [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] several hours or overnight for best flavor.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If you're in a hurry, bake at 375°F for 35–40 minutes.
* Buttermilk could be substituted with a tablespoon of [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] or [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] in milk.
* "Baker's Secret" is a brand of cooking spray that includes the flour.

recipes.title: Hongshao Rou (Red Braised Pork Belly)
recipes.original_wikitext:
{{recipesummary | category = Pork recipes | servings = 4 Servings | time = Prep: ~15 minutes
Cooking: 1 hour | difficulty = 3 }}{{recipe}} '''Hongshao rou''' (lit. red-cooked meat) is a traditional Chinese pork dish. It is a very popular homemade dish, but it is rarely found in Western restaurants. Often a family's exact recipe is a secret and passed down the generations. It consists of pork belly in a thick, sweet, dark sauce, simmered for a long time to soften the normally tough meat. Frequently other meats such as tripe or beef tendon are used in addition to the pork. ==Ingredients== *700 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] belly, [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]] *3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] *2 tbsp [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]] *350 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] pork or chicken [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] *1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] *2 tbsp dark [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]] *50 ml Shaoxing rice [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] *3 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pods *4 small [[Cookbook:Green Onion|spring onions]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] ==Procedure== #In a medium [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], over high heat, heat the oil and sugar together until the sugar melts and turns brown. #Add the cubed pork to the sugar and oil and brown all over. #Reduce the heat, add the stock, ginger, star anise, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine to the pan. #Cover tightly and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent it burning at the bottom. #Remove the lid and add the spring onions. #[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the sauce until only a thick, dark gravy is left. #The dish may be served now, but if possible, refrigerate for a day to allow the flavours to develop. #Serve with rice, garnish with sliced spring onion. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *Add 500 g sliced tripe. If the tripe was frozen, boil vigorously for about 40 mins until tender and not chewy. If fresh tripe is used (highly recommended) this is not required. Add to the pan about halfway through the simmering. *Add 250 g beef tendon, cut into small cubes. Boil vigorously for about 40 mins until translucent and not too chewy. Add this to the pan about halfway through the simmering. [[Category:Chinese recipes|Hongshao Rou]] [[Category:Recipes using pork]] [[Category:Recipes using star anise]] [[Category:Recipes using white sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using fresh ginger]] [[Category:Recipes using chicken broth and stock]] [[Category:Recipes using pork broth and stock]] [[Category:Recipes using vegetable oil]]
steps_original: In a medium saucepan, over high heat, heat the oil and sugar together until the sugar melts and turns brown.
Add the cubed pork to the sugar and oil and brown all over.
Reduce the heat, add the stock, ginger, star anise, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine to the pan.
Cover tightly and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent it burning at the bottom.
Remove the lid and add the spring onions.
Boil the sauce until only a thick, dark gravy is left.
The dish may be served now, but if possible, refrigerate for a day to allow the flavours to develop.
Serve with rice, garnish with sliced spring onion.
recipes.notes_source_wikitext:
*Add 500 g sliced tripe. If the tripe was frozen, boil vigorously for about 40 mins until tender and not chewy. If fresh tripe is used (highly recommended) this is not required. Add to the pan about halfway through the simmering.
*Add 250 g beef tendon, cut into small cubes. Boil vigorously for about 40 mins until translucent and not too chewy. Add this to the pan about halfway through the simmering.
